Revokes the session(s): the refresh token and any app refresh tokens in them stop working immediately, and the platform access token is rejected from then on — the API checks sid against the session table on every request, so logout is immediate, not “at access-token expiry”. Already-issued app tokens are not recalled (they’re verified locally by Applications, by design); they expire within 5 minutes. Logout does not by itself fire access.revoked — the User still has access; they’ve just signed out. Push devices registered under a revoked session become inactive, so a signed-out install stops receiving notifications.

57.title: Getting an app token
57.content: Embedded login is allowed for Applications staff create, which are either Substratal’s own or a concierge customer’s, so no unvetted third party ever handles a Substratal password. A self-registered Application is third-party: app-tokens refuses it with 403 embedded_login_not_allowed, and it must use the hosted flow. The hosted sign-in page must exist before any self-registered Application can go live. Requiring the hosted page from Phase 1 instead was considered and not chosen: it would make the MVP depend on a UI project. An app token is the per-Application JWT that Trust Model describes. Two ways to get one: . | Path | When | Calls | . | Embedded | The Application draws its own sign-in screen (any first-party app, native or web — the only option until the hosted page exists). | login → app-tokens. Refresh the platform session with token/refresh, then call app-tokens again. | . | Hosted + PKCE | The Application sends the user to Substratal’s hosted sign-in page (ships with the dashboard), and never sees the password. Required for third-party Applications. | App opens the authorization endpoint → hosted page calls oauth/authorization-codes → app calls oauth/token. Refresh with oauth/token (grant_type: refresh_token). | . Both paths produce the identical app token. Either way, issuance fails if the User doesn’t have active access to the Application right now: . | Error | Status | When | . | entitlement_required | 403 | Resolved entitlement status isn’t active (see Access Control). details.entitlement_status says what it is, including scheduled for a grant whose starts_at hasn’t arrived. | . | embedded_login_not_allowed | 403 | app-tokens only: the Application is self_registered, so it must use the hosted flow. | . | application_not_available | 409 | The Application’s review_status is suspended/rejected/pending_review — see Applications → review lifecycle. A state conflict, not a permission failure, so it’s the same 409 wherever this code appears. | . | tenant_suspended | 403 | The Application’s Tenant is suspended by the platform. See Tenancy. | . | account_suspended | 403 | The User is suspended. | . | test_user_expired | 403 | The test-mode User’s expires_at has passed. See Test-mode Users → Lifetime. | . The app token . { "iss": "https://api.substratalapps.com", "aud": "app_timetrack", "sub": "usr_01JAG3Z9X8QS3F6K2M4N5P6R7S", "sid": "ses_01JAG8K4Q9R0S1T2V3V4W5X6Y8", "org_id": null, "email": "jordan@example.com", "email_verified": true, "entitlement_status": "active", "effective_permissions": ["app.timetrack.export", "app.timetrack.manage_members"], "test_mode": false, "iat": 1730649600, "exp": 1730649900, "jti": "apt_01JAG8P1Q2R3S4T5U6V7W8X9Y0" } . | effective_permissions contains only this Application’s own app.<slug>.* keys — never platform permissions. See Access Control → Step 2. | org_id is the Organization whose org-wide grant provided access, if access came only through an Organization; null if the User has a personal Entitlement (personal wins for attribution when both exist). If multiple Organizations provide access and there’s no personal path, it’s the one whose grant was created first. Pass organization_id to app-tokens to pick a specific one explicitly. | sid lets an Application key its own local session to the hub session, so that an access.revoked webhook or a logout-everywhere can be matched to the right local session. | . POST /auth/app-tokens . // Request { "application_id": "app_timetrack" } . // Response — 200 { "token_type": "Bearer", "app_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6InNrXzIwMjYxMCJ9...", "expires_in": 300, "application_id": "app_timetrack" } . Bearer must be a platform access token (a User), not an API Key — 400 user_token_required otherwise. Optional organization_id selects which Organization’s grant to attribute org_id to; 403 entitlement_required if that Organization doesn’t actually include this User. The authorization endpoint . The hosted flow starts by sending the User’s browser (or, for a native app, the system browser) to the hosted sign-in page, a standard OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint: . GET https://auth.substratalapps.com/authorize ?response_type=code &client_id=app_timetrack &redirect_uri=com.substratal.timetrack%3A%2Foauth%2Fcallback &code_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM &code_challenge_method=S256 &state=af0ifjsldkj . It’s a web page, not part of the REST API, and it’s listed as authorization_endpoint in openid-configuration, so libraries like AppAuth discover it. The page signs the User in (creating a platform session if there isn’t one), then calls oauth/authorization-codes below with the same parameters and redirects to redirect_to. If client_id or redirect_uri isn’t valid it shows an error instead of redirecting, per OAuth 2.0; any later failure (no access, User cancelled) redirects back with error=access_denied and the original state. The page ships with the dashboard; until then only embedded login is available. POST /auth/oauth/authorization-codes . Called by Substratal’s hosted sign-in page (or the future dashboard’s “Launch” button) on the signed-in User’s behalf — not by the Application. // Request { "application_id": "app_timetrack", "redirect_uri": "com.substratal.timetrack:/oauth/callback", "code_challenge": "E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM", "code_challenge_method": "S256", "state": "af0ifjsldkj" } . // Response — 201 { "code": "ac_01JAG8R4S5T6U7V8W9X0Y1Z2A3", "expires_in": 60, "redirect_to": "com.substratal.timetrack:/oauth/callback?code=ac_01JAG8R4S5T6U7V8W9X0Y1Z2A3&state=af0ifjsldkj" } . redirect_uri must exactly match one of the Application’s registered redirect_uris (422 redirect_uri_not_registered); code_challenge_method must be S256 (plain is rejected, 422 validation_failed). An unknown or invisible application_id returns 404 application_not_found. The code is single-use, expires in 60 seconds, and belongs to the caller’s session: the app refresh token it’s later exchanged for is revoked whenever that session is. Access is checked here too, with the same errors as above, so a User without access is never redirected into the app holding a code. POST /auth/oauth/token . Called by the Application. A public-client endpoint: there’s no client secret, the PKCE verifier is the proof. It’s the one Auth endpoint that doesn’t need Substratal-Version, because standard OAuth libraries call it without custom headers (see Conventions → Versioning). Sending the header is fine. // Request — exchange an authorization code { "grant_type": "authorization_code", "client_id": "app_timetrack", "code": "ac_01JAG8R4S5T6U7V8W9X0Y1Z2A3", "code_verifier": "dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk", "redirect_uri": "com.substratal.timetrack:/oauth/callback" } . // Request — refresh { "grant_type": "refresh_token", "client_id": "app_timetrack", "refresh_token": "rtk_01JAG8S5T6U7V8W9X0Y1Z2A3B4" } . // Response — 200 { "token_type": "Bearer", "app_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...", "expires_in": 300, "refresh_token": "rtk_01JAG8T6U7V8W9X0Y1Z2A3B4C5", "refresh_token_expires_in": 2592000, "application_id": "app_timetrack" } . Accepts application/json and, for compatibility with standard OAuth client libraries (AppAuth, etc.), application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Errors on this one endpoint use the OAuth 2.0 shape ({"error": "invalid_grant", "error_description": "..."}) instead of this API’s usual envelope, again for library compatibility: invalid_grant (bad/expired/reused code or verifier mismatch), invalid_client (unknown client_id), unsupported_grant_type, and access_denied (access no longer active — error_description carries the entitlement_required detail). A refresh re-checks access every time — a refresh after revocation fails, which is what makes the hosted flow safe without a platform session.

58.title: Email verification
58.content: Transactional email (verification, password reset, invitations, MFA changes) is sent through Amazon SES in the same AWS account, so it adds no new sub-processor. Templates are Substratal-branded; an Application can set email_from_name and support_url so a message triggered from inside it names the app. A full per-Application custom domain and template is deferred. POST /auth/email/verify . // Request — token from the emailed link { "token": "emv_01JAG8V8W9X0Y1Z2A3B4C5D6E7" } . // Response — 204 . Sets email_verified: true (or, for a pending email change, swaps pending_email into email — see Users → PATCH). Token: single-use, 24-hour TTL. 400 token_invalid if expired, used, or unknown. POST /auth/email/verify/resend . // Request { "email": "jordan@example.com" } . // Response — 202, always, whether or not the email exists or is already verified . Limited to 3 per email per hour.

59.title: Password lifecycle
59.content: POST /auth/password/forgot . // Request { "email": "jordan@example.com" } . // Response — 202, always — never reveals whether the account exists . Sends a reset link (token pwr_…, single-use, 1-hour TTL) to an active User with a password identity. An SSO-only User gets an email explaining they sign in through their organization instead. Limited to 3 per email per hour. POST /auth/password/reset . // Request { "token": "pwr_01JAG8W9X0Y1Z2A3B4C5D6E7F8", "new_password": "a new long passphrase" } . // Response — 204 . Sets the new password (same policy as signup), marks the email verified (the User just proved control of it), revokes every session, and emails a “your password was changed” notice. Writes Audit Event user.password_reset. Errors: 400 token_invalid, 422 weak_password. POST /users/{id}/password . // Request { "current_password": "correct horse battery staple", "new_password": "a new long passphrase" } . // Response — 204 . Self only (an admin cannot set a User’s password — they can only trigger password/forgot on the User’s behalf). Revokes every other session; the calling session survives. Errors: 401 invalid_credentials (wrong current password), 422 weak_password. Writes user.password_changed.

60.title: Invitations
60.content: POST /users with status: "invited" (the default — see Users) or POST /organizations/{id}/members with an unknown email creates an invited User and emails an invitation link (token inv_…, single-use, 7-day TTL). POST /auth/invitations/accept . // Request { "token": "inv_01JAG8X0Y1Z2A3B4C5D6E7F8G9", "password": "correct horse battery staple", "display_name": "Jordan Alvarez" } . // Response — 200, an AuthSession . Creates the password identity, sets status: active and email_verified: true, and signs the User in. If the invitation came from an Organization, accepting it also accepts that pending membership (and any other pending memberships for this User), the same as …/members/me/accept. Errors: 400 token_invalid (expired invitations are re-sent with POST /users/{id}/invitation — see Users), 422 weak_password.

61.title: MFA (TOTP)
61.content: Optional and self-service for password identities. Meaningless for a method: sso identity, whose MFA policy belongs to the Organization’s own IdP (409 mfa_not_applicable if the User has no password identity). POST /users/{id}/mfa/totp — begin enrollment . // Request {} . // Response — 200 { "secret": "JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP", "otpauth_uri": "otpauth://totp/Substratal:jordan%40example.com?secret=JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP&issuer=Substratal&digits=6&period=30", "expires_in": 600 } . The client renders otpauth_uri as a QR code itself; the API never serves the secret through a URL. Enrollment is pending until confirmed; calling this again replaces a pending secret. 409 mfa_already_enabled if already confirmed. POST /users/{id}/mfa/totp/confirm . // Request { "code": "492039" } . // Response — 200 { "mfa_enabled": true, "recovery_codes": ["7hq2-kx9m-a4vd", "p3nc-8wz1-qt6r", "..."] } . Ten recovery codes, shown once — stored hashed. Writes user.mfa_enabled and emails a notice. 401 invalid_mfa_code on a wrong code; 409 mfa_enrollment_expired if the pending secret is older than 10 minutes. POST /users/{id}/mfa/totp/disable . // Request — a current TOTP code { "code": "492039" } . // Request — or a recovery code instead (exactly one of the two) { "recovery_code": "7hq2-kx9m-a4vd" } . // Response — 204 . Same fields as mfa/verify. Deletes the secret and every recovery code, writes user.mfa_disabled, and emails a notice. Existing sessions are kept. Errors: 401 invalid_mfa_code (wrong or reused code), 409 mfa_not_enabled (no confirmed TOTP to disable), and 429 too_many_attempts after 5 wrong codes in 15 minutes. DELETE /users/{id}/mfa/totp — support reset . Requires users.manage. For a User who has lost their device and their recovery codes; support verifies identity out of band first. Revokes every session. Writes user.mfa_reset. Destructive — see MCP Server → Tool annotations.

62.title: Sessions
62.content: GET /users/{id}/sessions . // Response — 200 { "data": [ { "id": "ses_01JAG8K4Q9R0S1T2V3V4W5X6Y8", "created_at": "2026-10-02T09:41:03Z", "last_seen_at": "2026-10-05T08:12:44Z", "expires_at": "2026-11-04T08:12:44Z", "ip_address": "203.0.113.24", "user_agent": "TimeTrack/2.4 (iOS 19.0)", "amr": ["pwd", "otp"], "current": true } ], "page": { "next_cursor": null, "has_more": false } } . expires_at is when the session ends if nothing else happens: the earlier of idle_expires_at (30 days after the last refresh, here 2026-10-05) and absolute_expires_at (90 days after creation, 2026-12-31). Each refresh pushes the idle expiry forward, never past the absolute one. DELETE /users/{id}/sessions/{sessionId} . 204. Same effect as logout for that one session, including deactivating the push devices it registered. revoked_reason is logout when the User revokes their own session, and admin when a users.manage caller does. POST /users/{id}/sessions/revoke-all . Signs a User out of every device in one call, for incident response on a compromised account that shouldn’t be suspended, or for a User who wants to sign out everywhere else. // Request — body optional { "keep_current": true } . // Response — 200 { "revoked": 3 } . | Who: the User themselves, or a users.manage caller. | Effect: every live session is revoked with revoked_reason: revoked_all, exactly as if each were revoked one at a time. Their refresh tokens and app refresh tokens stop working, access tokens from them are refused with 401 session_revoked, and the push devices they registered are deactivated. | keep_current: keeps the session making the call. Self only; anyone else sending it gets 422 validation_failed with the field code self_only. | Result: revoked counts the sessions revoked. 0 is still a success. | Audit: writes user.sessions_revoked, with the count and keep_current in after. | Destructive: see MCP Server → Tool annotations. | .

63.title: POST /auth/sso/{provider}/callback
63.content: Reserved. Returns 501 not_implemented until the SSO broker integration ships (see Native auth and per-Organization SSO). When live, it creates or matches a method: sso UserIdentity against the Organization’s SSOConnection and returns an AuthSession — SSO is a different way to obtain a session, not a different kind of session.

64.title: Signing keys (JWKS)
64.content: GET https://api.substratalapps.com/.well-known/jwks.json . { "keys": [ { "kty": "RSA", "kid": "sk_202610", "use": "sig", "alg": "RS256", "n": "0vx7agoebGcQSuu...", "e": "AQAB" } ] } . | RS256, 2048-bit keys, held in AWS KMS (the private key never leaves KMS — signing is a KMS Sign call). | Every token’s JWT header carries kid. Applications verify against the matching key and should cache the JWKS for up to 1 hour, re-fetching on an unknown kid. | Rotated every 90 days. A new key is published 7 days before it starts signing, and a retired key stays published for 7 days after its last use (longer than any token’s TTL), so a verifying Application never sees an unknown kid in normal operation. | Verification checklist for an Application: signature against JWKS, iss equals https://api.substratalapps.com, aud equals its own application_id, exp in the future (allow ≤60 s clock skew), entitlement_status is active. | . GET /.well-known/openid-configuration returns issuer, jwks_uri, authorization_endpoint (https://auth.substratalapps.com/authorize, see The authorization endpoint), token_endpoint (/auth/oauth/token), response_types_supported (code), grant_types_supported (authorization_code, refresh_token), and code_challenge_methods_supported (S256). It is metadata for standard libraries, not a claim of full OpenID Connect conformance (there is no id_token or userinfo endpoint).

65.title: Errors specific to this resource
65.content: | Code | Status | When | . | invalid_credentials | 401 | Login or password change with a wrong password/unknown email. | . | account_suspended | 403 | The User is suspended. | . | test_user_expired | 403 | A test-mode User whose expires_at has passed tried to sign in, refresh, or get an app token. | . | too_many_attempts | 429 | Account lockout after repeated failures. | . | email_taken | 409 | Signup with an email already in use. | . | weak_password | 422 | Password fails the policy. | . | token_invalid | 400 | Verification, reset, or invitation token is expired, used, or unknown. | . | invalid_mfa_code | 401 | Wrong or reused TOTP/recovery code. | . | mfa_token_invalid | 401 | MFA challenge expired or exhausted. | . | mfa_already_enabled / mfa_not_enabled / mfa_not_applicable / mfa_enrollment_expired | 409 | See MFA. | . | refresh_token_reused | 401 | A rotated refresh token was presented again — session revoked. | . | session_revoked | 401 | The session was logged out, reset, or the User suspended/deleted. | . | user_token_required | 400 | An endpoint that acts as a User was called with an API Key. | . | entitlement_required | 403 | App-token issuance for a User without active access. | . | application_not_available | 409 | App-token issuance for an Application not approved. | . | tenant_suspended | 403 | App-token issuance for an Application whose Tenant is suspended. | . | application_not_found | 404 | Unknown or invisible application_id on app-tokens or oauth/authorization-codes. | . | redirect_uri_not_registered | 422 | Authorization code requested for an unregistered redirect_uri. | . | not_implemented | 501 | SSO callback before the broker integration exists. | .

66.title: Billing
66.content: The Free/Standard subscription: a User subscribing to Standard for themselves, or an Organization subscribing for the members it covers, processed by Stripe. See Pricing for the tiers and rules. A third-party developer’s billing of their own users never touches this API (see Orders & Audit → Billing system of record). | How it fits together | Endpoints | The Subscription object | GET /subscriptions | GET /users/{id}/subscription | GET /organizations/{id}/subscription | PATCH /organizations/{id}/subscription | Checkout | Portal | Events | Errors specific to this resource | .

67.title: How it fits together
67.content: . | Free needs nothing. Every User is on Free from signup and has a platform-managed Entitlement to each free Application. | Subscribing sends the person through Stripe Checkout, using a URL from this API. A User subscribes for themselves; an org admin subscribes their Organization. | Payment methods, invoices, and cancellation are handled in the Stripe Customer Portal, again through a URL from this API. | A Stripe Customer is created for a User or Organization the first time they check out, not at signup. | Access follows the subscription. While a subscription covers someone, the platform keeps a source: subscription Entitlement for them to each standard Application. When it stops covering them, those Entitlements end. Applications hear about every change through the usual access.granted / access.revoked webhooks. | Business and Enterprise plans aren’t offered yet. Checkout for either returns 422 plan_requires_sales. | . Stripe tells this API about every change through its webhook. This API never takes card data, and a subscription’s status only changes in response to Stripe events. The handler is documented in infra/README.md → Stripe Billing.

68.title: Endpoints
68.content: | Method | Path | Requires | Purpose | . | GET | /subscriptions | billing.manage | Every subscriber’s subscription, filterable, for working the past_due list. | . | GET | /users/{id}/subscription | self, or billing.manage | A User’s plan, what covers it, and their own subscription. | . | POST | /users/me/billing/checkout-sessions | self, User token | Start a Stripe Checkout to subscribe yourself to Standard. | . | POST | /users/me/billing/portal-sessions | self, User token | Open the Stripe Customer Portal for your own subscription. | . | GET | /organizations/{id}/subscription | org_admin, or billing.manage | The Organization’s plan and subscription. | . | PATCH | /organizations/{id}/subscription | org_admin | Choose which members the subscription covers. | . | POST | /organizations/{id}/billing/checkout-sessions | org_admin, User token | Start a Stripe Checkout to subscribe the Organization to Standard. | . | POST | /organizations/{id}/billing/portal-sessions | org_admin or billing.manage, User token | Open the Stripe Customer Portal for the Organization’s subscription. | . Checkout and Portal act for a person, so they need a User token, not an API Key (400 user_token_required). An active member of the Organization who isn’t an org_admin gets 403; anyone else gets 404 organization_not_found.

69.title: The Subscription object
69.content: One row per subscriber, kept across lapses and resubscribes. { "id": "sbs_01JAGC3D4E5F6G7H8J9K011M2N", "subscriber_type": "organization", "user_id": null, "organization_id": "org_01JAGB2C3D4E5F6G7H8J9K0L1M", "plan": "standard", "status": "active", "current_period_start": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z", "current_period_end": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z", "cancel_at_period_end": false, "member_scope": "all_members", "member_overrides": null, "quantity": { "current": 31, "last_synced": 30, "last_synced_at": "2026-10-17T00:15:03Z" }, "unit_amount": 600, "currency": "usd", "test_mode": false, "created_at": "2026-09-30T18:02:11Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-17T00:15:03Z" } . | Field | Notes | . | id | sbs_ prefix. | . | subscriber_type | user (an individual subscription) or organization. Exactly one of user_id and organization_id is set. | . | plan | Always standard today. | . | status | active, trialing, past_due, canceled, unpaid, incomplete, incomplete_expired, or paused. Mirrors Stripe. active, trialing, and past_due cover their users with Standard; the rest don’t. A first Checkout that hasn’t completed yet is incomplete. A new Checkout keeps the row’s current status until Stripe reports the new subscription. A first Checkout that’s abandoned becomes incomplete_expired when Stripe expires the session, about 24 hours later. New values may be added; see Non-Functional Requirements → Versioning. | . | member_scope, member_overrides | Organization subscriptions only: all_members, allowlist, or denylist, with the same meaning as on org-wide Entitlements. null on an individual subscription. | . | quantity.current | Users billed, computed live. Always 1 for an individual subscription. For an Organization, its covered members: active Users with an active membership, included by member_scope, in the subscription’s own mode. See Pricing → What a “user” means for an Organization. | . | quantity.last_synced | What was last written to Stripe by the daily sync, which is what the next invoice charges for. | . | unit_amount | Cents per user per month. | . Invoices and receipts aren’t mirrored here. Stripe is the system of record for those, and the Portal shows them.

70.title: GET /subscriptions
70.content: GET /subscriptions?status=past_due&status=unpaid . // Response — 200 { "data": [ { "id": "sbs_01JAGC3D4E5F6G7H8J9K011M2N", "subscriber_type": "organization", "organization_id": "org_01JAGB2C3D4E5F6G7H8J9K0L1M", "status": "past_due", "...": "...", "user_email": null, "organization_name": "Acme Corp" } ], "page": { "next_cursor": null, "has_more": false } } . Every User’s and Organization’s subscription, for billing.manage only. Anyone else, including org admins and the subscribers themselves, gets 403. Each item is the Subscription object plus the subscriber for display: user_email on an individual subscription, organization_name on an Organization’s, and null for the other. A deleted User’s subscription is still listed, but user_email is null unless the caller also holds users.manage. Results are in the caller’s mode, most recently updated first, and cursor-paginated. This is what the API already stores. Revenue, invoices, and payment attempts stay in Stripe. | Filter | Meaning | . | status | Any of these statuses. Repeatable (?status=past_due&status=unpaid), up to 8. An abandoned first Checkout leaves an incomplete_expired row, so a console usually filters by status. | . | subscriber_type | user or organization. | . | cancel_at_period_end | true for subscriptions set to end at the period’s close, false for the rest. | . | current_period_end_before | ISO 8601. Subscriptions whose current period ends before this time. | . Ordering is by updated_at, which changes whenever Stripe reports a change. A subscription updated while you page through can move to the front, so it can be missed or seen twice in one pass.

71.title: GET /users/{id}/subscription
71.content: // Response — 200, a User covered by their Organization { "user_id": "usr_01JAGC3D4E5F6G7H8J9K0L1M2N", "plan": "standard", "plan_sources": [{ "type": "organization", "id": "org_01JAGB2C3D4E5F6G7H8J9K0L1M" }], "subscription": null } . plan and plan_sources are the same read-only fields as on the User object. subscription is the User’s own individual subscription, if they’ve ever started one, and null otherwise. A User covered both individually and by an Organization lists both sources, so a client can suggest cancelling the individual one. Nothing is refunded automatically.

72.title: GET /organizations/{id}/subscription
72.content: // Response — 200 { "organization_id": "org_01JAGB2C3D4E5F6G7H8J9K0L1M", "plan": "standard", "subscription": { "id": "sbs_01JAGC3D4E5F6G7H8J9K011M2N", "subscriber_type": "organization", "status": "active", "...": "..." } } . plan is standard while the subscription covers, and free otherwise. When a subscription exists, the response carries its ETag.

73.title: PATCH /organizations/{id}/subscription
73.content: // Request { "member_scope": "allowlist", "member_overrides": ["usr_01JAGC3D4E5F6G7H8J9K0L1M2N", "usr_01JAGD4E5F6G7H8J9K0L1M2N3P"] } . Changes which members the subscription covers. Only member_scope and member_overrides can be sent; anything else is 422 read_only_field. Every id in member_overrides must be a current active member (422 member_override_not_a_member). Send If-Match to avoid overwriting another admin’s change. Members gained or lost take effect immediately, firing access.granted / access.revoked, and the change is counted from the next daily sync. Returns 404 subscription_not_found if the Organization has never started a subscription.

74.title: Checkout
74.content: POST /users/me/billing/checkout-sessions (yourself) and POST /organizations/{id}/billing/checkout-sessions (an Organization). // Request (the Organization form also accepts member_scope and member_overrides) { "plan": "standard", "success_url": "https://hub.substratalapps.com/billing?checkout=success", "cancel_url": "https://hub.substratalapps.com/billing?checkout=cancelled", "member_scope": "all_members" } . // Response — 201 { "url": "https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_live_a1B2c3D4...", "expires_at": "2026-10-05T13:00:00Z" } . | plan must be standard. business or enterprise returns 422 plan_requires_sales. | Allowed when there’s no subscription yet, or the existing one is incomplete, incomplete_expired, canceled, or unpaid. Otherwise 409 subscription_exists, and the subscriber should use the portal instead. | The first Checkout creates the Subscription with status: incomplete, and writes subscription.created. | For an Organization, member_scope defaults to all_members, and Checkout’s quantity is the current covered-member count, at least 1. The individual form rejects member_scope and member_overrides. | Requires Idempotency-Key. success_url and cancel_url must be https. Stripe adds session_id. | Returning to success_url does not by itself mean the subscription started. Coverage begins when Stripe’s checkout.session.completed / customer.subscription.created webhook arrives, usually within seconds. Clients should poll the GET …/subscription endpoint until plan is standard. | Test mode. A test-mode User or Organization gets a test-mode subscription, which needs Stripe test mode. A deployment configured with a live Stripe key returns 409 test_mode_billing_unavailable. | .

75.title: Portal
75.content: POST /users/me/billing/portal-sessions and POST /organizations/{id}/billing/portal-sessions. // Request { "return_url": "https://hub.substratalapps.com/billing" } . // Response — 201 { "url": "https://billing.stripe.com/p/session/live_YWNjdF8x...", "expires_at": "2026-10-05T12:05:00Z" } . The Portal is configured to allow updating the payment method, viewing invoices, and cancelling at period end. Covered members are changed with PATCH …/subscription, not in the Portal. A subscriber who has never completed a Checkout gets 409 no_billing_account.

76.title: Events
76.content: Subscription changes write Audit Events with target type subscription: subscription.created, subscription.status_changed, and subscription.members_changed. There are no outbound webhook events for billing itself. What Applications need to know, who gained or lost access, arrives as access.granted / access.revoked, along with the entitlement.* events for the platform-managed rows.

77.title: Errors specific to this resource
77.content: | Code | Status | When | . | organization_not_found | 404 | {id} doesn’t resolve, or the caller isn’t a member and lacks billing.manage. | . | subscription_not_found | 404 | PATCH on an Organization that has never started a subscription. | . | plan_requires_sales | 422 | Checkout requested for business or enterprise. | . | subscription_exists | 409 | Checkout requested while a subscription is in force. | . | no_billing_account | 409 | Portal requested by a subscriber who has never completed a Checkout. | . | test_mode_billing_unavailable | 409 | Test-mode Checkout on a deployment that bills in Stripe live mode. | . | billing_unavailable | 503 | Stripe is unreachable, or billing isn’t configured. Retry-After is set. | . | user_token_required | 400 | Checkout or Portal called with an API Key, or me used without a User token. | . | idempotency_key_required | 400 | Checkout without an Idempotency-Key. | . | forbidden | 403 | Another User’s subscription without billing.manage, or an Organization endpoint by a member who isn’t an org_admin. | .

78.title: Changelog
78.content: What’s changed in this specification over time. Every decision is written into the page it governs, and recorded here as a dated entry. Add a new entry rather than editing an old one. Numbers like “#39” in older entries refer to the decision log the repository kept until 2026-10-18.

79.title: 2026-10-24 — The web Hub is at hub.substratalapps.com
79.content: The first-party web app, Substratal Hub, is served at https://hub.substratalapps.com instead of the planned dashboard.substratalapps.com, which was never served. | Links in verification, password-reset and invitation emails now point to https://hub.substratalapps.com (DASHBOARD_URL). | The CORS allow-list’s first-party origin is now https://hub.substratalapps.com. See NFR → CORS. | Billing examples and the legal documents name the new host. | . No API change: paths, requests and responses are the same.

80.title: 2026-10-23 — Legal documents and contact addresses
80.content: A new Legal section publishes the agreements at stable URLs, for app stores, sign-in providers, and payment providers that ask for them. Substratal Apps is operated by Composite Code LLC (Washington, USA). | Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, End User License Agreement for the six Hub apps, Developer and API Terms, Acceptable Use Policy, Data Processing Addendum (with the EU SCCs and UK Addendum by reference), Sub-processors, Cookie Notice, Account and Data Deletion, Security and Vulnerability Disclosure, and Copyright, Licenses and Trademarks. | Contact addresses privacy@, legal@ and security@substratalapps.com now receive mail, as does dmarc@ for DMARC reports. SES receives them on the apex domain and forwards them to the operator’s inbox (new mail-forward function; stored copies are deleted after 30 days). | Compliance now points to these documents: lawful basis and consent are covered by the Developer Terms, and the sub-processor agreements are in place. | .

81.title: 2026-10-23 — Checkout saves the billing address
81.content: Checkout now sets customer_update[address]: auto, so the billing address entered in Checkout is saved to the subscriber’s Stripe Customer. Stripe refuses a Checkout with automatic tax when the Customer has no address, and ours are created with only an email, so every Checkout would have failed against real Stripe (the test suite uses a fake). Found while setting up Stripe test mode. No API change. See infra/README.md → Objects and mapping.

82.title: 2026-10-23 — Abandoned Checkouts expire
82.content: A first Checkout that’s never completed no longer leaves its subscription incomplete forever. When Stripe expires the Checkout session (checkout.session.expired, about 24 hours later), the row becomes incomplete_expired, Stripe’s own status for a first payment that never completed, and subscription.status_changed is written. A row Stripe has already linked to a subscription is left alone, and so is one whose subscriber has a newer Checkout still open. The subscriber can check out again as before. Add checkout.session.expired by hand to the Stripe webhook endpoint’s events, in test and live mode; see infra/README.md → Webhook handling. No API or schema change.

83.title: 2026-10-23 — Optional counts on list responses
83.content: Console tables can show “1,204 users” for their current filters without paging everything (#53). openapi.yaml is now at 1.0.0-draft.11. No new operations, and no migration. | ?include=total adds page.total and page.total_capped to a list response. The count uses the list’s own filters and visibility, ignores cursor (every page reports the same total), and stops at 10,000: above that, total is 10000 and total_capped is true. Without the parameter, both fields are absent. Any other include value is 422 validation_failed. See Conventions → Pagination. | Supported on GET /users, /entitlements, /users/{id}/entitlements, /applications, /organizations, /organizations/{id}/members, /audit-events, /webhooks, /webhooks/{id}/deliveries, /api-keys, /roles, and /subscriptions, each declaring the shared Include parameter. PageInfo gains the two optional fields. | Cursors ignore include, so a cursor from a counted page works on an uncounted one and the other way round. | .

84.title: 2026-10-23 — A cross-subscriber subscription list
84.content: Billing admins can work the past_due list without going to Stripe (#57). openapi.yaml is now at 1.0.0-draft.10, with 125 operations. | GET /subscriptions lists every User’s and Organization’s subscription, for billing.manage only. Filters: status (repeatable), subscriber_type, cancel_at_period_end, and current_period_end_before. Cursor-paginated, most recently updated first. Each item is the Subscription object plus user_email or organization_name for display. Revenue and invoices stay in Stripe. No migration: the table holds one row per subscriber and already has a (status) index; an updated_at index can follow if query plans call for it. See Billing → GET /subscriptions. | .

85.title: 2026-10-22 — Browsers can read Deprecation and Sunset
85.content: Access-Control-Expose-Headers adds Deprecation and Sunset, so a web client can read them on a response to a deprecated version and tell its user to update, as Versioning already promised. No other change. See NFR → CORS.

86.title: 2026-10-22 — Browser CORS, a role filter on users, and sign out everywhere
86.content: Three gaps the management console needs (#38, #54, #51). openapi.yaml is now at 1.0.0-draft.9, with 124 operations. | CORS matches what’s built. NFR → CORS said only some GETs allowed the first-party origin and that an admin console would call through its own backend. In fact, allow-listed origins may call any endpoint with the signed-in person’s own User token, which is sound because a Bearer token isn’t sent automatically. The page now says so. | Browsers can now read Retry-After and Audit-Hot-Window-Start. | Preflights are cached for 2 hours instead of 10 minutes. | An API Key sent with an Origin header is refused with the new 400 api_key_in_browser, so a key pasted into a web page can’t be used from it. The Interactive Reference’s local “Try it out” takes a user token for the same reason. | . | GET /users?role_id= lists the Users holding any of the given Roles by explicit assignment. Repeatable, up to 20. An app-confined key may only name its own Application’s Roles (403 role_scope_mismatch). See Users → filters. | POST /users/{id}/sessions/revoke-all signs a User out everywhere, by the User or a users.manage caller, and returns {"revoked": n}. keep_current keeps the calling session, self only. New revoked_reason revoked_all and audit action user.sessions_revoked (migration 0012_sessions_revoked). Destructive. See Auth → Sessions. | .

87.title: 2026-10-22 — Audit Event exports
87.content: The audit log can be exported to a file. See API Reference → Audit → Exporting. openapi.yaml is now at 1.0.0-draft.8, with 123 operations. | POST /audit-exports takes the same filters as GET /audit-events, as body fields, plus format (ndjson or csv). It confines the caller to the same scope as the list, requires Idempotency-Key, and returns 202. A job writes the file, usually within a minute. Limited to 20 per caller per day. | GET /audit-exports/{id} shows the status, and once it’s ready, a download link signed for 15 minutes. Only the requester and audit.view can see an export. Files and records are deleted after 7 days. | New audit action audit.exported (target type audit_export), written when the file is ready, with the requester as actor. | Retention needed no new code. It’s already enforced: the one-year hot window, and the nightly archival of older events, shape-only, to indefinite cold storage (Audit log lifecycle). | Migration 0011_audit_exports. Infrastructure: a private exports bucket with a 7-day lifecycle rule, and an audit-exports schedule every minute. | .

88.title: 2026-10-22 — Self-service Application registration
88.content: POST /applications is open to developers, not just staff. See API Reference → Applications and The review lifecycle. openapi.yaml is now at 1.0.0-draft.7. | Any User with a verified email can submit an Application. It’s owned by the caller, or by an Organization they’re an org_admin of. It starts in pending_review, public, and standard, and the moderation fields are staff-only (403 moderation_field_forbidden). An unverified email is the new 403 email_not_verified. Each User can submit 10 a day. Staff creation is unchanged. | Applications gain self_registered (read-only, migration 0010_self_registered_apps). A self-registered Application is third-party, even once approved: . | POST /auth/app-tokens refuses it with the new 403 embedded_login_not_allowed, as Auth → Getting an app token already required once self-service shipped. It must use the hosted flow. | Only applications.manage can turn on its receives_platform_notifications, so platform security alerts never go out under an unvetted app. | . | Platform-managed Entitlements wait for approval. free and subscription rows are granted only to an Application that has been approved, and approving one grants them. Before this, a standard submission would have been granted to every Standard subscriber the moment it was created, firing access.granted to an unreviewed developer. | . Self-registered Applications still can’t go live until the hosted sign-in page exists.

89.title: 2026-10-22 — Test-mode User expiry implemented
89.content: Test-mode Users → Lifetime is built, as specified on 2026-10-20. openapi.yaml is now at 1.0.0-draft.6: . | User.expires_at, and expires_at on POST /auth/signup, POST /users, and PATCH /users/{id}. | user.expired in the webhook event and audit action enums, test_user_expired and test_user_extended in the access-event reasons, and test_user_expired in the device inactive reasons. | POST /auth/token/refresh and POST /auth/mfa/verify now declare 403, which they return for test_user_expired (and, for mfa/verify, account_suspended, which it already returned). | . A few behaviors the spec left implicit are now stated: . | An out-of-range or live-User expires_at is reported like any other field error: 422 validation_failed with the code in details.fields, not a separate details.reason. | A Platform access token whose test-mode User has expired gets 401 session_revoked, the same as a suspended User’s. Sign-in, refresh, MFA verification, and app-token issuance return 403 test_user_expired. | Extending a User the expiry sweep hasn’t processed yet fires no access.granted, since no access.revoked went out for them either. | Migration 0009_test_user_expiry sets every existing test-mode User’s expires_at to created_at + 30 days, when the purge would have removed them anyway. | .

90.title: 2026-10-22 — Version header declared in openapi.yaml; 405 for a wrong method
90.content: . | openapi.yaml declares Substratal-Version. Every versioned operation now carries the shared ApiVersion header parameter (Substratal-Version, enum 1) and documents its 400 (api_version_required, unsupported_api_version). Generated clients learn the header from the spec instead of needing it configured by hand. GET /health and POST /auth/oauth/token don’t declare it, because they’re exempt. Nothing changes on the wire: the API already required the header (Conventions → Versioning). | 405 method_not_allowed. Calling a path that exists with a method it doesn’t support (for example PUT /health) now returns 405 with an Allow header and details.allowed, instead of the catch-all 404 not_found. See Conventions → Errors. | .

91.title: 2026-10-21 — SCIM provisioning
91.content: An Organization’s identity provider can invite and remove its members with SCIM 2.0. See API Reference → SCIM. openapi.yaml is now at 1.0.0-draft.5, with 121 operations. | Setting it up: POST, GET, and DELETE /organizations/{id}/scim-token (org admin or organizations.manage). There’s one token per Organization, and its secret is shown once. New audit actions organization.scim_token_created and organization.scim_token_revoked. Migration 0008_scim_tokens. | /scim/v2 serves ServiceProviderConfig, ResourceTypes, and Users (list with a userName eq filter, create, get, put, patch, delete), in SCIM’s own response and error shapes. These endpoints follow RFC 7644, not openapi.yaml, like /.well-known, and are exempt from Substratal-Version: identity providers can’t add the header, and SCIM versions itself in the path. | The membership rules don’t change. Provisioning invites, so the person accepts before they join, whether or not they already had an account. Deprovisioning removes the membership, with access.revoked, and never touches the person’s own account. The last-org_admin guard applies. Writes are audited with actor type system and the token’s id. | Users only: no Groups, bulk, sorting, or ETags. Roles stay with org admins. | .

92.title: 2026-10-21 — Versioning rules spelled out
92.content: Clarifications to the header-based versioning below; nothing about the API’s behavior changed. | What counts as breaking is now listed in Non-Functional Requirements → Versioning: removing or renaming a field, endpoint, or parameter; changing a type or format; a new or newly required request field; a different status or error code for an existing condition; or a changed default or behavior. | Retirement. Deprecation (RFC 9745) and Sunset (RFC 8594) appear on responses to requests that name a deprecated version. After its Sunset date, requests naming it get 400 unsupported_api_version. | Two separate versions. The Substratal-Version request header and a webhook subscription’s payload api_version are independent, now stated on Conventions, Webhooks, and in the Glossary. | OpenAPI Specification no longer describes versions as URL prefixes, and Auth → POST /auth/oauth/token notes it needs no version header. | .

93.title: 2026-10-21 — The API version moves from the URL to a header
93.content: Breaking. The /v1 path prefix is gone. Every endpoint is now at the host root, and every request names its API version in a header instead: . POST https://api.substratalapps.com/users Substratal-Version: 1 . | Paths drop /v1. POST /v1/users is now POST /users, GET /v1/health is GET /health, and so on for every operation. /v1/… paths now return 404 not_found; there’s no alias or redirect. In openapi.yaml, the server URL is https://api.substratalapps.com, and the paths are unchanged. openid-configuration’s token_endpoint is /auth/oauth/token. | Substratal-Version is required. Versions are whole numbers, and 1 is the only one. A missing header is the new 400 api_version_required, and an unknown value is the new 400 unsupported_api_version. Both list the served versions in details.supported, and the check runs before authentication and every other validation. Every response echoes the version that served it, and the header is allowed and exposed for CORS. | Exempt: GET /health (for uptime monitors), POST /auth/oauth/token (standard OAuth libraries can’t add the header), and /.well-known/*. MCP clients don’t send it: the MCP server calls the API with the version its tools describe. | Unchanged: the deprecation policy (a breaking change is the next version, and the previous one keeps working for at least 6 months, with Deprecation and Sunset headers) and webhook payload versions (api_version dates, versioned independently). /.well-known, /mcp, and /internal are reserved and will never be resource names. | . See Conventions → Versioning. openapi.yaml is 1.0.0-draft.4. Older entries below keep the /v1/… paths that were current when they were written.

94.title: 2026-10-20 — Test-mode Users are time-limited
94.content: Test mode already never counted toward billing (decision #36, confirmed on 2026-10-18). Now every test-mode User expires, so a test account can’t stand in for a free production account. See Auth → Test-mode Users → Lifetime. | Users gain expires_at. It’s set on every test-mode User and is null on every live one. The default is 24 hours after creation. POST /v1/users with a satk_test_ key, and signup with "test_mode": true, accept expires_at for a shorter or longer run: at least 15 minutes away, and at most 30 days after creation, the existing test-data purge horizon. users.manage can move it with PATCH /v1/users/{id}, which also brings back an expired User that hasn’t been purged yet. | At expiry sign-in, refresh, and app-token issuance return the new 403 test_user_expired, and every token already issued stops working. No token’s exp is ever later than the User’s expires_at. The 5-minute entitlement-expiry sweep then revokes sessions and devices (reason test_user_expired), fires access.revoked (reason test_user_expired) and the new user.expired webhook, and writes the user.expired Audit Event. status, Entitlements, Roles, and memberships are unchanged. An expired test User isn’t a covered member of a test-mode subscription. | Test-mode API Keys, Organizations, and Applications don’t expire. The nightly 30-day purge is unchanged. | . Built on 2026-10-21; see the entry above.

95.title: 2026-10-18 — Push notifications implemented
95.content: Push Notifications is built: all 17 operations work, and none returns 501 any more. Nothing about the API’s shape changed. A few behaviors the spec left implicit are now stated: . | A User’s first session (at signup) never raises security.new_sign_in; there’s nothing yet to compare it with. | A device an app key registers or refreshes has session_id: null. | An unknown {provider} in a push-credential path is 404 push_credential_not_found. | A push-credential POST validates its fields before checking whether the provider is already configured, so an invalid body is 422 even when a credential exists. | Database Schema records each notification’s push counts on the notification itself, since deliveries are deleted after 30 days. | . Delivery shares the webhook queue, worker, and 1-minute sweep (see the repository’s infra/README.md → Push delivery), and a daily push-maintenance job runs the device and inbox retention rules. Locally, PUSH_BACKEND=log logs pushes instead of sending them.

96.title: 2026-10-18 — Billing options settled; decision log retired
96.content: . | Billing options (decision #31, the last open question): Standard is billed monthly in USD only, with no annual plan and no trial. Free is the way to try Substratal’s apps, and never needs a card. See Pricing → Stripe catalog. Either option can be added later as Stripe configuration, without an API change. | Push alerts and platform-managed access. The account.access_granted platform alert is raised only for access a developer or admin grants, never for platform-managed free or subscription Entitlements. Under subscriber billing, subscribing to Standard or publishing a free Application would otherwise have pushed one alert per app to every affected User. | The repository’s DECISIONS.md is retired. No decisions are open, every answer lives on the page it governs, and this Changelog records when each was made. The “Awaiting decision” callout style is removed from the site. | .

97.title: 2026-10-18 — Subscriber billing applied; decisions folded into the spec
97.content: Subscriber billing (decision #39, now resolved). The Free/Standard pricing from 2026-10-17 is now the API: . | Billing is rewritten. The four /v1/tenants/{id}/… billing endpoints are gone. In their place: GET /v1/users/{id}/subscription, POST /v1/users/me/billing/checkout-sessions and …/portal-sessions, and GET/PATCH /v1/organizations/{id}/subscription with the Organization’s own Checkout and Portal sessions. A new Subscription object (sbs_) belongs to a User or an Organization; Organizations choose which members it covers with member_scope. | Access stays Entitlement-based. Entitlement.source gains free and subscription, both platform-managed: every User gets free Applications at signup, and a covering subscription grants every standard Application. Admins can disable and re-enable them; anything else returns 409 entitlement_platform_managed. Entitlements gain subscription_id. | | Applications gain access_tier (free | standard, default standard), a moderation field with an access_tier list filter. Users gain plan and plan_sources. | . | Removed: Tenant plan, subscription_status, and restricted (and the plan/restricted list filters); the per-plan caps on Applications, AppRoles, webhooks, and seats; 402 subscription_required; member_decision: seat_limit; plan_does_not_allow_tier; GET /v1/tenants/{id}/usage. plan_limit_reached is reserved for future business and enterprise limits. | Audit: subscription.created, subscription.status_changed, and subscription.members_changed (target type subscription) replace tenant.plan_changed and tenant.subscription_status_changed. The audit hot window is one year for every Tenant. | New workflows: A User subscribes to Standard and An Organization subscribes to Standard for its members. | . Decisions folded into the spec. #32–#34, #36, #37, and #40 are confirmed as proposed and written into the pages they govern: Organization and Tenant scoping in the data-access layer (NFR → Multi-tenancy), inline Stripe webhook processing, JWKS caching without CloudFront at Tier 0 (NFR → Service-level objectives), test mode and subscriptions (Pricing), audit immutability by trigger (NFR → Audit), and the push notification defaults (Push Notifications). Only #31, annual plans and a Standard trial, is still open.

98.title: 2026-10-17 — Push notifications and the notification inbox
98.content: New: Push Notifications, so an Application can send a User alerts and other updates without building its own push stack, and the platform can tell a User about their account. | Devices. A client registers its APNs, FCM, or Web Push token per Application (POST /v1/users/{id}/devices), with its user token or through its backend’s app key. A Device is tied to the session that registered it, so signing out stops its pushes. A token a provider reports as gone deactivates the device automatically. | Push credentials. Each Application’s owner configures its own APNs key, FCM service account, or Web Push (VAPID) key pair under /v1/applications/{id}/push-credentials. Key material is write-only and KMS-encrypted, and only a person can manage it, the same rule as API Keys. | Sending. POST /v1/users/{id}/notifications, with a new app-confined permission, notifications.send. Every send lands in the User’s inbox, whether or not a push goes out, and push.status says what happened. The recipient must have active access to the Application, and a User who sets notifications.push: false in Settings (globally, or for one app) gets the inbox item without the push. | The inbox. List, count unread, mark read, unread, or archived, and mark many read at once. Kept 90 days. | Platform alerts. A fixed catalog of security.* and account.* notifications (new sign-in, password or email changed, MFA disabled, token reuse, organization invitation, access granted), pushed to the devices of Applications that opt in with the new receives_platform_notifications field. | Everywhere else it touches: 17 operations under a new Notifications tag in openapi.yaml (info.version 1.0.0-draft.3), new id prefixes (dvc_, pcr_, ntf_, ndl_), webhook events (device.registered, device.deactivated, device.deleted, notification.push_failed, push_credential.failed), audit actions (push_credential.created/updated/deleted, device.deleted), Database Schema, a new Domain Model → Notifications page, rate limits and an SLO in Non-Functional Requirements, the export and erasure cascade, Apple, Google, and browser push services as sub-processors, two new Workflows, and the Roadmap. | . The defaults this rests on (opt-in platform pushes, no broadcast endpoint yet, the per-recipient limit, 90-day retention, no quiet hours yet) are listed for confirmation in decision #40. None blocks building. Until the reference implementation builds the feature, every Notifications operation returns 501 not_implemented.

99.title: 2026-10-17 — Free and Standard pricing; OpenAPI Specification section
99.content: Pricing (decision #38). Pricing now has two tiers, paid by the people who use Substratal’s apps rather than by the Application owner: . | Free gives every User the Applications, features, and services Substratal designates as free. No card is required. | Standard is $6 per user per month for access to every Application and service. A User subscribes for themselves, or an Organization subscribes for the members it covers. | Business and Enterprise pricing, tailored to an Organization’s needs, tenancy, and data location, comes later. Until then, isolated and dedicated_region tenancy are reserved for it. | . The previous Starter / Team / Enterprise plans, their per-Tenant limits, and Tenant restricted mode are retired from Pricing. Billing system of record, the Glossary, the Roadmap, and NFR → Audit log lifecycle are updated to match. decision #31 now covers only annual plans and a Standard trial, and #35 is withdrawn. The API changes that implement the new model aren’t applied yet. They’re proposed in decision #39, and every affected page (Billing, Tenancy, Entitlements, Applications, Organizations, Webhooks, Conventions, Access Control, Database Schema, Workflows) carries an “Awaiting decision” callout until then. openapi.yaml is unchanged. OpenAPI Specification. A new top-level section for developers building against the API: OpenAPI Specification explains how to read, download, validate, and generate clients from openapi.yaml. The Interactive Reference renders the document with Swagger UI, including “Try it out” against a local devserver.

100.title: 2026-10-06 — Implementation-driven openapi.yaml fixes
100.content: The first implementation’s contract tests validate every response against openapi.yaml, and found places where the YAML disagreed with the prose (which is authoritative). Each is now fixed in the YAML; no behavior described on any page changed: . | ApplicationWrite.slug: pattern used a negative lookahead (?!platform$) that RE2-based JSON Schema validators (Go, Rust) can’t compile; now ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,63}$, with platform documented as reserved in the description (the server still rejects it). | RoleCreate/Role.description: now nullable, matching Domain Model → Role (“string, nullable”); a Role created without one has none. | ApplicationWrite/ApplicationSummary description and icon_url: now nullable, matching the Applications page’s own POST response example ("icon_url": null); both are optional on create. | GET /organizations/{id}/entitlements: declared the filters its prose already promised (“same filters as GET /v1/entitlements”: application_id, status, order_id, ends_before, include_inactive). | GET /tenants: declared owner_user_id and owner_organization_id, which Tenancy → GET /v1/tenants already listed for tenants.manage. | . Questions the build surfaced where the spec was silent or self-contradictory are recorded as decision #32–#37.

101.title: 2026-10-06 — Domain Model and API Reference review
101.content: A review of every Domain Model and API Reference page against each other, the database schema, and openapi.yaml. Every fix is stated on the page it affects. Security and correctness . | Signup no longer completes an invitation. Signing up with an invited User’s email used to activate that account with no invitation token, handing whatever was pre-attached to it to anyone who knew the address. It now returns 409 email_taken (details.reason: "invitation_pending") and re-sends the invitation. See Auth → Signup. | Organization invitations are now pending until accepted. Since anyone can create an Organization, adding members by email used to reveal whether an address had an account, and that account’s name. Adds by email now create a pending membership whose response looks the same either way. Adds by user_id are restricted to organizations.manage. A new POST /v1/organizations/{id}/members/me/accept endpoint and audit action organization.member_invited support this. | Test-mode Users can sign in. Uniqueness is per mode, so the email-keyed auth endpoints now take test_mode (Auth → Test-mode Users). include_test is gone: test and live rows never cross, under any parameter. | Role ids can’t collide. The slug now appears verbatim in Role ids (it never contains _), and platform is a reserved slug. Application ids are documented as app_<slug>, the second derived-id exception after Role. | Typed-settings view and index names are now built from hashes, so they always fit Postgres’s 63-byte limit. | Support can read for investigations. Reading AppProfile/AppSettings/global Settings past the access gate now needs users.list (which support holds), not users.manage (which it doesn’t). | Application owners can grant Entitlements with their own User token, personal and org-wide alike, confined to their Application exactly like its app key. | . Contradictions resolved . | One rule for soft-deleted vs. terminal records (Conventions → Filtering): terminal records stay fetchable; soft-deleted Users 404 except to users.manage. Flags unified on include_inactive. | Webhook DELETE drops queued deliveries (Conventions said otherwise). | Audit Events: the erasure cascade’s redaction is now documented as one of two scheduled jobs allowed to touch an event; actor.via_api_key_id (never defined) is removed; user.updated and role_assignment targets are defined precisely. | Erasure: a soft-deleted User can be restored (deleted → active) or have erasure requested by users.manage; the cascade also clears memberships and member_overrides. Export and the cascade are described accurately (export includes global Settings; erasure leaves it). | application_not_available is 409 everywhere. The implicit default_app_role is listed only while access is active. | Profile.locale is a read-only mirror of Settings.locale. Settings resolution is described as the two disjoint chains it actually is. | Credential storage (webhook secrets are KMS-encrypted, recovery codes Argon2id), order_id examples, and the supporting-entity count/ER diagram corrected. Every example id is now a valid ULID. | . Specified (previously missing) . | Entitlements: disabled → expired, renewal conflicts, a scheduled resolved status for future starts_at and an access.granted reason entitlement_started, and which excluded org rows a member sees. | 403 tenant_suspended; 409 idempotency_key_in_flight in the global table; the plan_limit_reached details shape, with usage keys renamed to match (app_roles, webhooks). | The hosted flow’s authorization endpoint (authorization_endpoint in OIDC discovery); MFA disable with a recovery code; what a session’s expires_at means. | SSO: a domain is claimable by one active connection platform-wide, and SSOConnection has no API until the broker ships. Webhooks: request scope, per-attempt signing, webhook.test delivery rules, and a payload versions table. | Missing error codes added to each resource’s table; missing fields added to the Domain Model (User, AppProfile, Application, Role, Tenant) and the database schema (test_mode, created_at, version, current_period_start). | .
