167.title: webhook_subscriptions, webhook_events, webhook_deliveries
167.content: webhook_subscriptions ( id text primary key, -- whk_... scope text not null, -- 'platform' or an application_id tenant_id text references tenants(id), -- null for platform scope url text not null, events text[] not null, -- or '{*}' description text, api_version text not null, -- e.g. '2026-10-05' secret_ciphertext text not null, -- KMS-encrypted: the API must sign with it, so it can't be a hash previous_secret_ciphertext text, -- set for 24h after a rotation previous_secret_expires_at timestamptz, status text not null default 'healthy' check (status in ('healthy','unhealthy','disabled')), consecutive_failures int not null default 0, unhealthy_since timestamptz, test_mode boolean not null default false, created_at timestamptz not null default now(), updated_at timestamptz not null default now(), version integer not null default 1 ); webhook_events ( -- the transactional outbox id text primary key, -- wev_... type text not null, application_id text, payload jsonb not null, test_mode boolean not null default false, created_at timestamptz not null default now(), dispatched_at timestamptz -- set once fan-out to subscriptions is enqueued ); webhook_deliveries ( id text primary key, -- dlv_... subscription_id text not null references webhook_subscriptions(id) on delete cascade, event_id text not null references webhook_events(id), attempt int not null, status text not null check (status in ('pending','succeeded','failed')), response_status int, duration_ms int, error text, -- first 1 KB only next_retry_at timestamptz, created_at timestamptz not null default now() ); . A webhook_events row is inserted in the same transaction as the change it describes. A dispatcher (SQS-fed, see infra/README.md) fans it out to matching subscriptions. That makes “every committed change produces its event” structural rather than best-effort. Events and deliveries are deleted after 30 days. Indexes: (dispatched_at) where dispatched_at is null; (subscription_id, created_at desc) and (next_retry_at) where status = 'pending' on deliveries.

168.title: push_credentials, devices, notifications, notification_deliveries
168.content: The tables behind Push Notifications. See Domain Model → Notifications for what each field means. push_credentials ( id text primary key, -- pcr_... application_id text not null references applications(id), tenant_id text not null references tenants(id), provider text not null check (provider in ('apns','fcm','web_push')), config jsonb not null, -- non-secret: team_id/key_id/topic | project_id/client_email | subject/vapid_public_key secret_ciphertext text not null, -- KMS-encrypted: the .p8 key | the service-account JSON | the VAPID private key status text not null default 'active' check (status in ('active','failed')), failure_reason text, failed_at timestamptz, last_used_at timestamptz, created_at timestamptz not null default now(), updated_at timestamptz not null default now(), version integer not null default 1, unique (application_id, provider), check ((status = 'failed') = (failed_at is not null)) ); devices ( id text primary key, -- dvc_... user_id text not null references users(id), application_id text not null references applications(id), tenant_id text not null references tenants(id), session_id text references sessions(id) on delete set null, -- null when an app key registered it provider text not null check (provider in ('apns','fcm','web_push')), environment text check (environment in ('production','sandbox')), token_hash text not null, -- sha256 of the token, or of the web_push endpoint: the dedup key token_ciphertext text not null, -- KMS-encrypted token, or the whole PushSubscription JSON token_hint text not null, -- last 4 characters name text check (char_length(name) <= 100), app_version text check (char_length(app_version) <= 50), status text not null default 'active' check (status in ('active','inactive')), inactive_reason text check (inactive_reason in ('unregistered','session_revoked','user_suspended','user_deleted','test_user_expired','stale','limit','credential_removed')), deactivated_at timestamptz, last_registered_at timestamptz not null default now(), last_delivery_at timestamptz, test_mode boolean not null default false, created_at timestamptz not null default now(), updated_at timestamptz not null default now(), version integer not null default 1, check ((provider = 'apns') = (environment is not null)), check ((status = 'inactive') = (inactive_reason is not null)), check ((status = 'inactive') = (deactivated_at is not null)) ); notifications ( id text primary key, -- ntf_... user_id text not null references users(id), application_id text references applications(id), -- null for a platform alert tenant_id text references tenants(id), -- set exactly when application_id is source text not null check (source in ('application','platform')), category text not null check (category ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z0-9_]+)*$' and char_length(category) <= 64), priority text not null default 'normal' check (priority in ('normal','high')), title text not null check (char_length(title) between 1 and 120), body text check (char_length(body) <= 1000), data jsonb not null default '{}', action_url text check (char_length(action_url) <= 2048), badge integer check (badge between 0 and 99999), sound text check (sound = 'default'), collapse_key text check (char_length(collapse_key) <= 64), ttl_seconds integer not null default 86400 check (ttl_seconds between 0 and 2419200), push_requested boolean not null default true, push_status text not null check (push_status in ('queued','sent','failed','skipped')), skip_reason text check (skip_reason in ('push_not_requested','push_disabled','no_devices','no_credentials','credential_failed','expired')), push_devices_targeted integer not null default 0, -- the push summary; kept here because deliveries push_devices_sent integer not null default 0, -- are deleted after 30 days and notifications push_devices_failed integer not null default 0, -- after 90 sender_type text not null check (sender_type in ('api_key','user','system')), sender_id text not null, -- key_..., usr_..., or 'system'; not a foreign key, since it spans tables read_at timestamptz, archived_at timestamptz, test_mode boolean not null default false, created_at timestamptz not null default now(), updated_at timestamptz not null default now(), version integer not null default 1, check ((source = 'platform') = (application_id is null)), check ((application_id is null) = (tenant_id is null)), check ((push_status = 'skipped') = (skip_reason is not null)), check (source = 'platform' or category !~ '^(security|account|billing)\.') ); notification_deliveries ( id text primary key, -- ndl_... notification_id text not null references notifications(id) on delete cascade, device_id text references devices(id) on delete set null, provider text not null check (provider in ('apns','fcm','web_push')), status text not null default 'pending' check (status in ('pending','sent','failed','skipped')), attempts int not null default 0 check (attempts between 0 and 4), provider_status int, error text, -- the provider's reason code, or 'timeout' next_attempt_at timestamptz, sent_at timestamptz, test_mode boolean not null default false, created_at timestamptz not null default now() ); . The notifications row and its notification_deliveries rows are inserted in the same transaction, one delivery per Device eligible at that moment. That’s the same transactional outbox as webhook_events: a worker picks up pending deliveries (nudged through SQS after commit, plus a sweep), so a committed send can never lose its push. A platform alert is inserted in the same transaction as the action that raises it, before any session revocation that action makes. push_credentials is Application configuration, so like applications it isn’t covered by the test/live Row-Level Security policy. It has no test_mode column, because one credential serves both modes. The other three tables carry test_mode and are covered. devices, notifications, and notification_deliveries hold personal data: the hard-delete cascade deletes a User’s rows from all three. Indexes: unique (application_id, provider, token_hash, test_mode) on devices, which is what makes registration an upsert keyed on the token; (user_id, application_id) where status = 'active' (fan-out at send time, and the 20-device cap); (session_id) where session_id is not null (deactivate on session revocation); (last_registered_at) where status = 'active' (the 270-day stale sweep); (deactivated_at) where status = 'inactive' (deleting devices 30 days after deactivation). On notifications: (user_id, created_at desc, id) where archived_at is null (the default inbox list); (user_id, application_id, created_at desc) (an app key’s view, and the per-recipient rate limit’s count of the last hour); (user_id) where read_at is null and archived_at is null (unread counts); (created_at) (the 90-day purge). On notification_deliveries: (next_attempt_at) where status = 'pending' (the worker’s queue) and (notification_id). Deliveries are deleted after 30 days and notifications after 90. Both purges run nightly.

185.title: 1. Definitions
185.content: “Data Protection Law” means all laws that apply to processing Customer Personal Data under the agreement, including the EU GDPR, the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018, Swiss data-protection law, and US state privacy laws such as the CCPA/CPRA. “Customer Personal Data” means personal data that we process on Customer’s behalf: the data of Customer’s end users and members held in Customer’s Applications or Organizations. “Controller,” “processor,” “data subject,” “personal data breach,” “processing,” “service provider,” and “supervisory authority” have the meanings given in Data Protection Law.

186.title: 2. Roles and instructions
186.content: Customer is the controller (or a processor for its own customers), and we are the processor (and a “service provider” or “processor” under US state laws). We process Customer Personal Data only on Customer’s documented instructions, which are the agreement, Customer’s configuration and use of the Service, and API calls Customer makes, unless the law requires otherwise, in which case we’ll tell Customer first unless the law forbids it. We’ll tell Customer if we believe an instruction violates Data Protection Law.

187.title: 3. Details of processing
187.content: |   |   | . | Subject matter and duration | Providing the Service, for the term of the agreement and the deletion period below | . | Nature and purpose | Hosting, storing, authenticating, authorizing, transmitting, and deleting data to provide user accounts, access control, settings, organizations, storage, notifications, and audit records | . | Data subjects | Customer’s end users, members, and administrators | . | Categories of data | Identifiers and contact details (name, email), credentials (password hashes, encrypted second-factor secrets), session and device data (IP address, user agent, push tokens), access and role assignments, settings and application data Customer chooses to store, notifications, and audit records | . | Special categories | None intended. Customer must not store special-category or protected health data in the Service unless we have agreed to it in writing. | .

188.title: 4. Our obligations
188.content: . | Confidentiality. People authorized to process Customer Personal Data are bound by confidentiality. | Security. We implement the technical and organizational measures in Annex 1 and keep them at least as protective as they are today. | Sub-processors. Customer authorizes the sub-processors on Sub-processors. We impose data-protection terms on each that are at least as protective as this DPA, and remain responsible for them. We’ll announce a new sub-processor on that page and in the Changelog at least 30 days before it starts processing Customer Personal Data; Customer may object on reasonable data-protection grounds within that period, and if we can’t address the objection, Customer may terminate the affected Service. | Data subject requests. We provide self-service export (GET /users/{id}/export) and erasure (POST /users/{id}/erasure-requests) and will otherwise reasonably help Customer respond. If we receive a request directly, we’ll refer it to Customer. | Assistance. We’ll reasonably help Customer with data-protection impact assessments and consultations with supervisory authorities, as they relate to the Service. | Breach notification. We’ll notify Customer without undue delay, and in any case within 48 hours, after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer Personal Data, with the information Customer needs to meet its own obligations, including the GDPR’s 72-hour notification. | US state law. We won’t sell or share Customer Personal Data, retain, use, or disclose it outside our direct business relationship with Customer or for any purpose other than providing the Service, or combine it with personal data from other sources except as Data Protection Law permits. | .

189.title: 5. Deletion and return
189.content: Customer can export and delete Customer Personal Data through the API during the term. When the agreement ends, we delete Customer Personal Data within 30 days, and remove it from backups on their normal rotation, except where the law requires us to keep it. Audit records keep only the fact that an action happened once their personal details are removed (see Data retention).

190.title: 6. Audits
190.content: We’ll make available the information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with this DPA, including written answers to security questionnaires and, when available, third-party audit reports. If that isn’t enough to meet a regulator’s requirement, Customer may audit our compliance once a year, with 30 days’ notice, at its own cost, under confidentiality, and without disrupting the Service.

191.title: 7. International transfers
191.content: Customer Personal Data is processed in the United States. For transfers from the EEA, the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914), Module Two (controller to processor) or Module Three (processor to processor) as applicable, are incorporated by reference, with Clause 7 included, option 2 of Clause 9 with the notice period in section 4, no optional language in Clause 11, governing law and courts of Ireland in Clauses 17 and 18, and Annexes completed by section 3 and Annex 1 of this DPA. For the UK, the UK International Data Transfer Addendum applies; for Switzerland, the SCCs apply with the Swiss FDPIC as the competent authority. If the SCCs conflict with this DPA, the SCCs prevail.

192.title: 8. Liability and order of precedence
192.content: Each party’s liability under this DPA is subject to the limitations in the agreement, to the extent Data Protection Law allows. If this DPA conflicts with the rest of the agreement on processing Customer Personal Data, this DPA prevails.

193.title: Annex 1: Technical and organizational measures
193.content: . | Encryption: TLS for data in transit; encryption at rest for the database, backups, and storage; application secrets and second-factor secrets encrypted with keys in AWS KMS; passwords hashed with Argon2id. | Access control: short-lived signed access tokens; role- and permission-based authorization on every request; least-privilege IAM for every component; production access limited to authorized personnel with multi-factor authentication. | Isolation: test and live data separated by database row-level security; per-Application and per-Organization scoping enforced in the data-access layer. | Logging and monitoring: audit records of administrative and security-relevant actions; security event logging and alarms. | Resilience: managed infrastructure; database storage replicated across availability zones, with automated daily backups kept 7 days and deletion protection. | Development: changes are reviewed and tested in CI before deployment, and infrastructure is defined as code. | Incident response: a documented breach-notification commitment, with audit records as the forensic source. | Deletion: self-service export and erasure, with erasure completed 7 days after a request. | .

194.title: Entitlements
194.content: The record behind “turn an app on/off for a user.” If this site has one load-bearing entity, it’s this one. | What it represents | Fields . | source | . | Platform-managed Entitlements | Org-wide entitlements: scoping members in or out . | Attribution | Worked example: who gets access through one org grant | . | Status transitions | This is the endpoint everything else points back to | Example | .

195.title: What it represents
195.content: The join between a User (or Organization) and an Application: does this party own this app, and is it currently switched on. Independent of Role — see Access Control for why that split matters.

196.title: Fields
196.content: | Field | Type | Notes | . | id | string | ent_ prefix. | . | user_id | string, nullable | Set unless this is an org-wide grant. | . | organization_id | string, nullable | Set for an org-wide grant: source: org_seat, or an Organization’s source: subscription row. See source below. | . | application_id | string |   | . | status | enum | active | disabled | expired | revoked. See Access Control → Step 1. | . | source | enum | purchase | trial | admin_grant | org_seat | free | subscription. The last two are platform-managed. | . | order_id | string, nullable | An opaque reference into the developer’s own billing system, typically set when source: purchase. Up to 255 characters. It isn’t a resource of this API; see Orders & Audit → Order. It can be set once and is then immutable. | . | subscription_id | string, nullable | Set on source: subscription rows: the Subscription that grants them. Read-only. | . | starts_at | timestamp | May be in the future (up to 1 year). Until it passes, the row is active but isn’t an access path yet; the resolved status for a User whose only path hasn’t started is scheduled. | . | ends_at | timestamp, nullable | Set for trials and fixed-term subscriptions. | . | disabled_reason | string, nullable | Why the row last left active. It’s required on any transition to disabled or revoked (for example billing_dispute, refunded, chargeback, tos_violation), and cleared automatically on re-enable. | . | member_scope | enum, nullable | Only meaningful on an org-wide row. On an Organization’s subscription row it mirrors the Subscription’s own member_scope. all_members (default) | allowlist | denylist. See Org-wide entitlements: scoping members in or out. | . | member_overrides | array, nullable | Only meaningful when member_scope is allowlist or denylist. Array of user_ids (up to 1,000, all current active members) this org-wide grant’s default is flipped for. Removing someone from the Organization removes them from this list too. A soft-deleted User stays listed, so a restore brings back the same standing; the erasure cascade removes them. | . | test_mode | boolean | Created by a test-mode key. | . | created_at, updated_at | timestamp | updated_at changes on every write. Webhook consumers use it to discard out-of-order events. | . Uniqueness: at most one live (active or disabled) developer-granted personal row per (user, Application), and one live developer-granted org row per (Organization, Application). Separately, at most one live platform-managed row per holder, Application, and source. A developer grant and a platform-managed row can coexist, and either one alone gives access. expired and revoked rows are history and don’t block a new grant. source . | Value | When it’s used | . | purchase | Standard commerce path — see Workflows → Purchase → access. | . | trial | Time-boxed access, no payment yet. ends_at drives the transition to expired. | . | admin_grant | Support/sales gave access directly — comped account, early access, internal testing. Usually no order_id. | . | org_seat | Granted to an Organization as a whole. Members get access through it because they belong to that Organization, which holds a grant to the app. It doesn’t have to own the app. user_id is null — the grant is modeled at the org level and resolved per-member at read time, per member_scope below. | . | free | Platform-managed. Every User’s access to each Application whose access_tier is free. Always personal. | . | subscription | Platform-managed. Granted while a Standard Subscription covers its holder, to each standard Application: personal for an individual subscription, org-wide for an Organization’s. | .

197.title: Platform-managed Entitlements
197.content: free and subscription rows implement Pricing. The platform creates and ends them; no API call does: . | When | What the platform does | . | A User is created | Grants them a free row to each free Application. | . | A Subscription starts covering its holder (active, trialing, or past_due) | Grants a subscription row to each standard Application: personal for a User, org-wide with the Subscription’s member_scope for an Organization. | . | A Subscription stops covering (canceled, unpaid, incomplete_expired, paused) | Sets ends_at to now on its rows, which expires them. Resubscribing revives the same row while it’s still live, or grants a new one. | . | An org admin changes the Subscription’s covered members | Updates member_scope / member_overrides on the Organization’s rows. | . | An Application is created approved, is approved, or its access_tier changes | Grants or ends rows for that Application to match. Only an Application that has been approved (approved, or suspended, since suspension doesn’t cascade) gets them: never a submission still in review or rejected. | . | Hourly | Repairs anything that drifted (subscription-access job). | . Each change writes the usual Audit Event with actor system, fires the matching entitlement.* webhook, and fires access.granted / access.revoked for every User whose resolved access actually changed. People can do exactly one thing to a platform-managed row: someone with entitlements.manage (or the Application’s owner) can disable it with a disabled_reason, and re-enable it. The platform never re-enables a row an admin disabled. Every other change (revoke, ends_at, member_scope, delete) returns 409 entitlement_platform_managed, and granting one through the API returns 422 invalid_source.

198.title: Org-wide entitlements: scoping members in or out
198.content: An org-wide (source: org_seat) Entitlement’s default is that every current and future member of the Organization gets the app — no per-member row to create or maintain. member_scope narrows that default, giving an org admin (OrganizationMembership.role: org_admin) a whitelist/exclusion list rather than all-or-nothing: . | member_scope | Who gets this grant | . | all_members (default) | Every current and future member — unchanged behavior. | . | allowlist | Only the members listed in member_overrides. Everyone else in the Organization does not get this app through this grant. | . | denylist | Every member except the ones listed in member_overrides. | . This governs only this one Organization’s own grant. It does not reach into, and cannot revoke, a member’s separate Entitlement to the same Application sourced some other way (a personal purchase, a trial, an admin_grant) — see Access Control → Organization vs. User precedence for why that scoping is deliberate. A User’s actual access to an app is always the union of every active path available to them; excluding someone from one Organization’s seat grant only removes that path. Attribution . Reading a member’s own entitlements (GET /users/{id}/entitlements) surfaces why an org-sourced row is what it is, not just the resulting status — so anyone pulling a User’s data can see which Organization is responsible: . { "id": "ent_01JAGD4E5F6G7H8J9K011M2N30", "user_id": null, "organization_id": "org_01JAFZ8Y7X6W5V4V3T2S1R0Q9P", "application_id": "app_invoicer", "status": "active", "source": "org_seat", "member_scope": "denylist", "member_overrides": ["usr_01JAG3Z9X8QS3F6K2M4N5P6R7S"], "granted_via": { "organization_id": "org_01JAFZ8Y7X6W5V4V3T2S1R0Q9P", "member_decision": "excluded" } } . granted_via is computed per member at read time (it’s not stored — member_scope + member_overrides on the org-wide row is the source of truth) and only appears when the caller is asking about a specific member’s resolved standing, e.g. via GET /users/{id}/entitlements, rather than the raw org-wide grant itself. member_decision is included or excluded (left out by member_scope/member_overrides). Rows with excluded are listed, so a member can see why they don’t have access, but they’re never an access path. Note that status above is the org-wide grant’s own status (active), not this member’s access; their resolved access comes from effective-permissions. Worked example: who gets access through one org grant . Acme Co. (org_01JAFZ8Y7X6W5V4V3T2S1R0Q9P) has three active members: Jordan, Sam, and Riley. Riley also bought Invoicer personally. Here is the same Invoicer org grant under each member_scope, with member_overrides: ["usr_…Sam"]: . | member_scope | Jordan | Sam | Riley | . | all_members (overrides ignored) | included → access | included → access | included → access (two paths) | . | allowlist | excluded → no access | included → access | excluded, but access via the personal Entitlement | . | denylist | included → access | excluded → no access | included → access (two paths) | . Switching the grant from all_members to denylist with Sam listed fires one entitlement.member_scope_changed event (audit and webhook) for the grant, plus access.revoked (reason: org_grant_changed) for Sam only. Switching from all_members to allowlist fires access.revoked for Jordan only: Riley loses the org path but keeps access through the personal Entitlement, so their resolved access doesn’t flip and nothing fires for them. Riley’s GET /users/{id}/apps/app_invoicer/effective-permissions under allowlist shows both paths: . { "allowed": true, "entitlement_status": "active", "access_paths": [ { "source": "purchase", "entitlement_id": "ent_01JAG6R2N7HX0K9T4V5W6Y7Z8A", "status": "active" }, { "source": "org_seat", "entitlement_id": "ent_01JAGD4E5F6G7H8J9K011M2N30", "status": "active", "organization_id": "org_01JAFZ8Y7X6W5V4V3T2S1R0Q9P", "member_decision": "excluded" } ], "...": "..." } .

199.title: Status transitions
199.content: grant │ ▼ admin disables ┌────────┐ ends_at passes (system) ┌─────────────────│ active │──────────────────────┐ ▼ └────────┘ ▼ ┌──────────┐ re-enable ▲ ▲ renew (new ends_at) ┌─────────┐ │ disabled │──────────────┘ └───────────────────────│ expired │ └──────────┘──── ends_at passes (system) ───────────►└─────────┘ │ active / disabled / expired │ └───────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘ ▼ refund, chargeback, ToS ┌─────────┐ │ revoked │ terminal — grant a new Entitlement instead └─────────┘ . | From | To | Who | Notes | . | (new) | active | entitlements.manage (platform or the app’s own key), or the app’s owner | A starts_at in the future is allowed. The row is active, but access doesn’t resolve until starts_at (resolved status scheduled). When it passes, the same 5-minute sweep fires access.granted (reason: entitlement_started), and access resolution treats starts_at ≤ now as started immediately. | . | active | disabled | entitlements.manage; an org admin for their own Organization’s org_seat row | Reversible. disabled_reason required. | . | disabled | active | same | Restores exactly the prior state. | . | active | expired | system | ends_at passed. A 5-minute sweep writes it, and access resolution treats ends_at ≤ now as expired immediately. | . | disabled | expired | system | ends_at passed while disabled. The same sweep writes it. disabled_reason is kept as history. No access.* event fires, since a disabled row wasn’t granting access. | . | expired | active | entitlements.manage, or the app’s owner | Renewal, with a new future ends_at or null. Rejected with 409 entitlement_already_exists if a newer live (active/disabled) row now exists for the same holder and Application; renew or change that one instead. | . | active / disabled / expired | revoked | entitlements.manage | Terminal. disabled_reason required. | . Wherever this table says entitlements.manage, the Application’s owner (with a User token) can do the same for that Application’s own rows, exactly as its app-confined key can. See Applications → Who can manage an Application’s catalog entry. disabled is the soft, reversible toggle: support flips it back to active, and everything (Roles, AppProfile, AppSettings for that app) is exactly as it was. revoked means the underlying ownership is gone, so restoring access later means a brand-new Entitlement, not reinstating this one. A hard DELETE is reserved for removing a grant made in error. It’s limited to rows without order_id that are less than 24 hours old. See API Reference → Entitlements.

200.title: This is the endpoint everything else points back to
200.content: PATCH /entitlements/{id} { "status": "disabled", "disabled_reason": "billing_dispute" } . is the entire “turn this app off for this user” feature. See API Reference → Entitlements for the full endpoint list, and Workflows → Admin turns an app off for a user for the end-to-end sequence including the Audit Event and webhook it triggers.

202.title: Entitlements
202.content: The on/off switch for a user’s access to an app. See Domain Model → Entitlements for the full field reference and status lifecycle. | Endpoints | The Entitlement object | GET /users/{id}/entitlements | POST /users/{id}/entitlements | GET /entitlements | GET /entitlements/{id} | PATCH /entitlements/{id} — the toggle | DELETE /entitlements/{id} | Errors specific to this resource | .

203.title: Endpoints
203.content: | Method | Path | Requires | Purpose | . | GET | /users/{id}/entitlements | self, entitlements.manage, or app-confined entitlements.manage/users.list | A user’s entitlements, personal and org-sourced — what a dashboard renders as “your apps.” | . | POST | /users/{id}/entitlements | entitlements.manage (platform or app-confined), or the Application’s owner | Grant a personal Entitlement. | . | GET | /entitlements | entitlements.manage (platform or app-confined), or the Application’s owner | Cross-user list: “who has app X.” | . | GET | /entitlements/{id} | self, a member of the holding Organization, entitlements.manage, or the Application’s owner | Fetch one Entitlement. | . | PATCH | /entitlements/{id} | entitlements.manage (platform or app-confined), or the Application’s owner; an org admin may change only status (active ⇄ disabled) and member_scope/member_overrides on their own Organization’s org_seat row | The toggle. Change status, term, or org-grant scope. | . | DELETE | /entitlements/{id} | entitlements.manage (platform or app-confined), or the Application’s owner | Hard-remove a grant made in error. | . Org-wide grants are created through POST /organizations/{id}/entitlements. Once created, they’re read and changed through /entitlements/{id} like any other Entitlement. App-confined callers. An app-scoped API Key holding entitlements.manage can do everything on this page, but only for Entitlements whose application_id is its own Application. That includes its own Application’s org-wide grants (a developer’s backend reflecting a team purchase). Anything else returns 404 entitlement_not_found, so other apps’ rows aren’t revealed. This is how an Application developer reflects their own billing outcome. See Workflows → Purchase → access. The Application’s owner (its owner_user_id, or an org_admin of owner_organization_id) can do the same with their own User token, confined to their Application in exactly the same way. Wherever this page says entitlements.manage, the owner is included for their own Application’s rows. That’s what lets a developer fix a grant by hand from the dashboard without minting a key.

208.content: Returns the Entitlement object. Self may fetch their own personal rows, plus org rows of Organizations they belong to (with granted_via). An org admin may fetch their Organization’s rows.

209.title: PATCH /entitlements/{id} — the toggle
209.content: Platform-managed rows (source: free or subscription) accept only status (active ⇄ disabled) and disabled_reason, from entitlements.manage or the Application’s owner. Anything else returns 409 entitlement_platform_managed, and so does DELETE. See Platform-managed Entitlements. // Request — turn off { "status": "disabled", "disabled_reason": "billing_dispute" } . // Request — turn back on { "status": "active" } . // Request — the developer's customer refunded { "status": "revoked", "disabled_reason": "refunded" } . // Request — extend a trial { "ends_at": "2026-11-02T12:00:00Z" } . // Request — convert a trial to a purchase { "source": "purchase", "order_id": "sub_1Q9z8X7c6V5b4N3m", "ends_at": null } . // Request — on an org-wide grant, narrow who it applies to { "member_scope": "denylist", "member_overrides": ["usr_01JAG3Z9X8QS3F6K2M4N5P6R7S"] } . // Response — 200, the full updated Entitlement (here, after "turn off") { "id": "ent_01JAG9F4Q1W2E3R4T5Y6V7J809", "user_id": "usr_01JAG3Z9X8QS3F6K2M4N5P6R7S", "organization_id": null, "application_id": "app_invoicer", "status": "disabled", "source": "purchase", "order_id": "sub_1Q9z8X7c6V5b4N3m", "starts_at": "2026-03-02T09:00:00Z", "ends_at": null, "disabled_reason": "billing_dispute", "member_scope": null, "member_overrides": null, "test_mode": false, "created_at": "2026-03-02T09:00:00Z", "updated_at": "2026-09-30T16:22:41Z" } . Status transitions. Anything not listed here returns 409 invalid_status_transition. | From → to | Allowed for | Notes | . | active → disabled | entitlements.manage; org admin on org_seat | disabled_reason required (422 disabled_reason_required), 1–255 characters. Reversible. | . | disabled → active | same | disabled_reason is cleared automatically. | . | active/disabled/expired → revoked | entitlements.manage only (not org admins) | Terminal. disabled_reason is required and records why (“refunded”, “chargeback”, “tos_violation”). | . | expired → active | entitlements.manage only | Renewal. Only valid together with an ends_at in the future, or ends_at: null. Returns 409 entitlement_already_exists (with details.existing_entitlement_id) if a newer live row now exists for the same holder and Application. | . | active → expired | system only | Happens when ends_at passes. A sweep runs every 5 minutes, and access resolution also treats ends_at <= now as expired immediately, so expiry is never late. | . | disabled → expired | system only | ends_at passed while the row was disabled. Same sweep. disabled_reason is kept. No access.* event, since a disabled row wasn’t granting access. | . | revoked → * | nobody | Grant a new Entitlement instead. | . Other writable fields: . | Field | Rule | . | ends_at | Changeable on active/disabled/expired rows. Setting it in the past on an active row expires it on the next sweep. | . | source | Only trial → purchase (a conversion). Any other change returns 422 immutable_field. | . | order_id | Settable while null. Changing an existing value returns 422 immutable_field, so it stays a stable reconciliation key. | . | member_scope, member_overrides | org_seat rows only (422 not_an_org_grant otherwise). Every listed user must be a current member (422 member_override_not_a_member). | . | starts_at, user_id, organization_id, application_id | Read-only (422 read_only_field). | . Effects: every change writes an Audit Event and emits a webhook in the same transaction. The action/event is the target status (entitlement.granted, entitlement.disabled, entitlement.revoked), or entitlement.updated for term/source/order changes, or entitlement.member_scope_changed for scope changes. Separately, access.revoked / access.granted fire once per affected user whose resolved access to the Application actually flips. For an org grant that can mean many users. A user who still has another active path, such as a personal Entitlement, gets no access.* event. See Webhooks → Event types. disabled/revoked transitions are destructive for MCP / restrict_destructive purposes. Send If-Match when two operators might act on the same row. See Conventions → Concurrency. revoked is terminal. You can’t PATCH a revoked entitlement back to active; grant a new one instead. disabled is the reversible switch, and re-enabling restores exactly the prior state (Roles, AppProfile, AppSettings untouched).

210.title: DELETE /entitlements/{id}
210.content: // Response — 204 . Removes the record entirely. It’s reserved for correcting a grant made by mistake (wrong user, wrong app, duplicate). For every other case, such as a real purchase ending or a real admin decision to cut off access, use PATCH with status: revoked or disabled so the history survives. | Requires entitlements.manage (platform or app-confined). | Rejected with 409 entitlement_order_linked whenever order_id is set, whoever the caller is, whatever restrict_destructive is set to. An order-linked Entitlement is a real financial record, never “a mistake” in this endpoint’s sense. | Rejected with 409 entitlement_too_old if the row is more than 24 hours old. After a day it has very likely been relied on, so revoke it instead. | Writes Audit Event entitlement.deleted (the audit trail of the correction survives, even though the row doesn’t), emits the entitlement.deleted webhook, and emits access.revoked if it was the user’s only active path. | Destructive: a restrict_destructive key gets 403 destructive_operation_restricted. | .

211.title: Errors specific to this resource
211.content: | Code | Status | When | . | entitlement_not_found | 404 | {id} doesn’t resolve, or isn’t visible to the caller. | . | entitlement_already_exists | 409 | A live (active/disabled) personal row already exists for this user and app. | . | invalid_status_transition | 409 | See the transition table. | . | invalid_source | 422 | source: org_seat, free, or subscription on the personal grant endpoint. | . | ends_at_required | 422 | A trial without ends_at. | . | disabled_reason_required | 422 | disabled/revoked without a reason. | . | immutable_field | 422 | Changing source (other than trial → purchase) or an existing order_id. | . | not_an_org_grant | 422 | member_scope/member_overrides on a personal row. | . | member_override_not_a_member | 422 | A member_overrides id isn’t a current member. | . | application_not_available | 409 | The Application isn’t approved, or is internal and the caller isn’t platform. | . | entitlement_platform_managed | 409 | PATCH on a free or subscription row that does anything but disable or re-enable it, or DELETE on one. See Platform-managed Entitlements. | . | idempotency_key_required | 400 | POST without an Idempotency-Key. | . | read_only_field | 422 | PATCH touches starts_at, user_id, organization_id, or application_id. | . | tenant_suspended | 403 | Any write when the Application’s Tenant is suspended. | . | validation_failed | 422 | For example starts_at more than 1 year ahead, or ends_at not after starts_at. | . | entitlement_order_linked | 409 | DELETE on a row with order_id. | . | entitlement_too_old | 409 | DELETE on a row older than 24 hours. | .

223.title: Read these three pages first
223.content: . | Domain Model — the nouns. Ten entities, most of them small. Skim the overview table, then come back to individual entity pages as you need them. | Access Control — the one algorithm that matters: allow(user, application, permission). Read this once so every other API reference page can skip repeating it. | . Everything past that is detail you’ll reach for as needed, not a reading order. Each page has a request/response example you can copy. | Check Workflows for the end-to-end sequence your feature is probably a step in — most features are one step in a flow that’s already documented there, not a new flow. | If your feature needs a downstream app (one of the Applications built on this platform, hosted independently) to know a user’s access, read Trust Model before inventing your own session/token scheme. | .

226.title: What’s deliberately not here
226.content: This is an API-first specification. There is no UI, no page layout, no client framework decision made anywhere in this site — that’s out of scope by design, planned as a separate project once the API exists. Don’t infer a UI shape from anything here. Billing/payment processing is each Application developer’s own concern, not something this API runs — see Orders & Audit → Billing system of record. App-specific business logic lives in the Application itself, outside this API entirely. Don’t design payment flows or app business logic here.

227.title: Glossary
227.content: Precise definitions for every term used across this site. If a page uses a capitalized term (Entitlement, AppRole) without defining it inline, it means exactly what’s written here. Access path . One way a User reaches an Application: their own personal Entitlement, or an org-wide grant from an Organization that includes them. Resolved access is the union of every active path. See Access Control. Access tier . Which Pricing tier unlocks an Application: free (every User) or standard (Users covered by a Subscription). See Applications. API Key . A long-lived service credential (satk_live_…/satk_test_…), scoped to the platform or to one Application. An app-scoped key can only ever touch its own Application’s rows. See API Keys. API version . The version of the REST API a request is written against, sent as a whole number in the required Substratal-Version header. 1 is the only one so far. Unrelated to a webhook payload version. See Conventions → Versioning. App token . The short-lived (5-minute) JWT an Application verifies locally, with aud set to that Application. Carries entitlement_status and effective_permissions. See Auth → The app token. Application . (also “App”) One developer’s separately-hosted app (web, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, …) that uses Substratal Apps for its users, settings, organizations, tenancy, and storage. This is its catalog entry. See Domain Model → Applications. AppProfile . Per-app identity data for one user — e.g. a display handle meaningful only inside that one app. Distinct from the global Profile. AppRole . A Role scoped to one Application, defined by that app’s own catalog entry rather than by the platform. See Domain Model → Roles & Permissions. AppSettings . Per-app configuration for one user, layered over that user’s global Settings and the Application’s declared defaults. See Workflows → Settings resolution. Audit Event . An immutable record of who changed what access, when. See Domain Model → Orders & Audit. Device . One install of an Application on one device, signed in as one User, with the APNs, FCM, or Web Push token that reaches it (dvc_…). Tied to the Session that registered it, so signing out stops its pushes. See Push Notifications → Devices. Effective permissions . The resolved set of Permissions a user holds for a given Application — the union of the permissions on their app-scoped Roles for that app (explicit assignments plus the app’s default_app_role), and empty unless the User and their Entitlement are both active. Only that app’s own app.<slug>.* keys ever appear; platform Roles govern the hub, not apps. See Access Control. Entitlement . The join record between a User (or Organization) and an Application: do they own it, and is it currently switched on. The record behind “turn an app on/off for a user.” See Domain Model → Entitlements. Hub . Shorthand used throughout this site for Substratal Apps itself — the platform this API belongs to. MCP . Model Context Protocol — the standard this site’s AI-agent-facing tool-call interface implements. See MCP Server. Introduces no new authorization model of its own; see Authentication — no new model. Notification . One alert or update to one User (ntf_…), from an Application or from the platform. Pushed to the User’s Devices when it can be, and always kept in their inbox for 90 days. See Push Notifications. Order . Not an entity of this API. It’s the developer’s own commerce record, in their own billing system. An Entitlement carries only an opaque order_id reference to it. See Domain Model → Orders & Audit. Organization . A domain/grouping object for Users — a company, or a group within a company — used to organize shared admin standing and group-wide Application access. Decoupled from infrastructure placement; see Tenant and Tenant vs. Organization. Pulled into Phase 2; see Organizations. OrganizationMembership . The join record between a User and an Organization, carrying that User’s standing within that one Organization (org_admin or member) and whether it’s pending (invited, not yet accepted) or active — a User can hold this for any number of Organizations at once. See Domain Model → Users & Organizations. Payload version . The shape of a webhook’s payloads, a date pinned on each subscription as api_version (currently 2026-10-05) and moved forward only by its owner. Unrelated to the API version. See Webhooks → Payload versions. Permission . An atomic, checkable capability, written as a dotted key (billing.manage, app.timetrack.export). Never assigned directly to a user — always granted through a Role. Plan . The subscription tier covering a User: free or standard. A User is on Standard through their own subscription or an Organization’s. Business and Enterprise plans come later. Independent of Tier. See Pricing. Platform alert . A Notification the platform raises itself about the User’s account, such as a new sign-in or a changed password. Its category is from a fixed catalog under security. and account.. See Push Notifications → Platform alerts. PlatformRole . A Role that applies across the whole hub rather than one Application — superadmin, support, billing_admin, member. Profile . Global, cross-app identity and contact data for a User — name, avatar, email, locale. Distinct from AppProfile. Push credential . An Application’s own key for one push provider: an APNs .p8 key, an FCM service account, or a Web Push (VAPID) key pair (pcr_…). Write-only and KMS-encrypted. Providers deliver only for the app a token was issued to, so every Application brings its own. See Push Notifications → Push credentials. Role . A named bundle of Permissions. Either a PlatformRole or an AppRole. Seat . A covered member of an Organization with a Standard subscription: a distinct, active, non-test-mode member included by the subscription’s member selection. The unit an Organization is billed on, $6 each per month. See Pricing. Session . One successful login (ses_…). Every refresh token and app token minted from it carries its id as sid, and revoking it ends them all. See Auth → Sessions. Settings . Global, cross-app configuration for a User — locale, timezone, notification preferences. Distinct from AppSettings. Subscription . A User’s or an Organization’s Standard subscription (sbs_…), billed through Stripe at $6 per covered user per month. While it covers its holder, the platform grants subscription Entitlements to every standard Application. See API Reference → Billing. Tenant . The infrastructure-placement and data-isolation boundary for an Application’s data — it belongs to the owner of the Application’s catalog entry, and isn’t billed. shared (default), isolated, or dedicated_region. Not the same thing as Organization — see Tenant vs. Organization. See Domain Model → Tenancy. Tier . Where a Tenant’s data physically lives: shared, isolated, or dedicated_region. Independent of Plan. The non-shared tiers are reserved for business and enterprise pricing, which isn’t offered yet. User . A person with an account on Substratal. One identity, used everywhere in the hub and, via the Trust Model, in every app they launch from it. Webhook . A signed HTTPS POST the hub sends an Application when something changes. access.revoked and role.removed are required subscriptions. See Webhooks.

228.title: Domain Model
228.content: Ten core nouns, each small on purpose — the complexity in this system is in how they relate, not in any single one’s field list — plus twelve supporting join, credential, and request records that make the many-to-many relationships, multi-method auth, and support workflows actually work without a bigger table.

229.title: Overview
229.content: | Entity | What it represents | . | User | A person with an account on Substratal. One identity, used everywhere. | . | Organization | A domain/grouping object — a company, or a group within one — for Users. Decoupled from infrastructure placement; see Tenancy. Pulled into Phase 2. | . | Tenant | The infrastructure-placement and data-isolation boundary for one Application owner’s data — shared, isolated, or dedicated-region. See Tenant vs. Organization. | . | Application | A catalog entry for a developer’s app, built on this platform for its user/org/tenancy/settings/storage layer. | . | Role / Permission | A named bundle of capabilities, scoped to the platform or to one app. | . | Entitlement | The on/off record: does a User own an Application, and is it currently switched on. | . | Profile / AppProfile | Identity/display data — global, and per-app. | . | Setting / AppSettings | Configuration — global, and per-app, layered over app defaults. | . | Order | Not stored here. The developer’s own commerce record. An Entitlement carries only an opaque order_id reference to it. | . | Audit Event | An immutable log of who changed what access, when. | .

230.title: Supporting entities
230.content: Each of these is a join or credential record behind one of the relationships above — real rows in the schema, just not independent concepts the way the ten above are: . | Entity | Joins | What it represents | . | UserIdentity | User ↔ login method | How a User actually authenticates — password or sso — since a User can hold more than one at once. See Auth → Native auth and per-Organization SSO. | . | SSOConnection | Organization ↔ identity provider | One Organization’s federated-login configuration, referenced by its members’ sso-method UserIdentity rows. | . | OrganizationMembership | User ↔ Organization | Which Organizations a User belongs to, and their standing (org_admin/member) in each. | . | UserRoleAssignment | User ↔ Role | Which Roles a User holds, platform-wide or scoped to one Application. | . | Session | User ↔ login | One successful login. Every refresh token and app token minted from it carries its id (sid), so revoking it ends them all. | . | TierChangeRequest | Tenant ↔ migration | One support-run request to move a Tenant to a more isolated tier. | . | ErasureRequest | User ↔ erasure | A scheduled right-to-erasure request: at most one per User, run 7 days after it’s made. | . | Webhook subscription | Application (or the platform) ↔ endpoint | Where an Application’s events (or, for a platform subscription, every event) are delivered, plus the delivery log. | . | API Key | Application (or the platform) ↔ service | A long-lived credential for a backend or agent, scoped to one Application or to the platform, with no User behind it. | . | Device | User ↔ Application install | One install of an Application, signed in as one User, with the APNs, FCM, or Web Push token that reaches it. See Notifications. | . | PushCredential | Application ↔ push provider | An Application’s own APNs key, FCM service account, or Web Push key pair, which the platform signs its pushes with. | . | Notification | User ↔ message | One alert or update to one User, from an Application or the platform: the unit of sending, and the User’s inbox item. Its per-device deliveries are the push outbox. | .

231.title: How they relate
231.content: erDiagram USER ||--o{ ENTITLEMENT : holds USER ||--o{ ORGANIZATION_MEMBERSHIP : "belongs via" ORGANIZATION ||--o{ ORGANIZATION_MEMBERSHIP : "has members via" ORGANIZATION ||--o{ ENTITLEMENT : "holds (org-wide)" APPLICATION ||--o{ ENTITLEMENT : "granted via" USER ||--o{ APPLICATION : owns ORGANIZATION ||--o{ APPLICATION : "owns (alt.)" USER ||--o| TENANT : "owns (alt.)" ORGANIZATION ||--o| TENANT : "owns (alt.)" TENANT ||--o{ APPLICATION : places ENTITLEMENT ||--o| ORDER : "traces to" USER ||--|| PROFILE : "has (global)" USER ||--o{ APP_PROFILE : "has, per app" APPLICATION ||--o{ APP_PROFILE : scopes USER ||--|| SETTINGS : "has (global)" USER ||--o{ APP_SETTINGS : "has, per app" APPLICATION ||--o{ APP_SETTINGS : scopes USER }o--o{ PLATFORM_ROLE : assigned USER }o--o{ APP_ROLE : "assigned, per app" APP_ROLE }o--|| APPLICATION : scopes PLATFORM_ROLE ||--o{ PERMISSION : grants APP_ROLE ||--o{ PERMISSION : grants USER ||--o{ AUDIT_EVENT : "is target of" APPLICATION ||--o{ API_KEY : "scopes (app keys)" APPLICATION ||--o{ WEBHOOK_SUBSCRIPTION : "scopes (app subscriptions)" USER ||--o{ DEVICE : "signs in on" APPLICATION ||--o{ DEVICE : "installed as" APPLICATION ||--o{ PUSH_CREDENTIAL : configures USER ||--o{ NOTIFICATION : receives . The relationship worth internalizing before reading further: Entitlement and Role are independent axes. Entitlement answers “can this user reach this app at all, right now.” Role answers “once inside, what can they do.” See Access Control for how the two combine on every request.

232.title: ID format
232.content: Every entity has an opaque, stable id, prefixed by type for readability (a Stripe-style convention): usr_, uid_, ssc_, ses_, org_, tnt_, tcr_, app_, role_, ent_, evt_, whk_, wev_, dlv_, key_, dvc_, pcr_, ntf_, ndl_. Most are the prefix plus a ULID. IDs are never reused and never encode meaning beyond the type prefix, with two deliberate exceptions: an Application’s id is app_<slug> and a Role’s is derived from its scope and name. See Conventions → IDs. Building the actual database, not just calling the API? Database Schema has the Postgres-level types, constraints, and indexes behind every entity above.

237.content: When a document changes materially, we update its effective date, announce it in the Changelog, and, for the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, notify account holders by email or in the Hub at least 30 days before the change takes effect, unless the change is required sooner by law. Earlier versions stay available in this site’s git history.

238.title: API Reference
238.content: Resource-oriented REST, JSON, versioned by the Substratal-Version request header (currently 1). Read Conventions first — every other page here assumes it. The same contract is available as OpenAPI 3.1 in OpenAPI Specification, with an interactive Swagger UI reference. | Group | Covers | . | Conventions | Base URL, auth header, pagination, idempotency, error shape, ID format. | . | Auth | Signup, login, MFA, sessions, password and email lifecycle, invitations, and app tokens (embedded, and hosted + PKCE). | . | Users | Account lifecycle. | . | Profiles | Global and per-app identity data. | . | Settings | Global and per-app configuration. | . | Applications | The app catalog. | . | Entitlements | Grant, toggle, revoke access to an app — the on/off switch. | . | Roles & Permissions | Assign/remove roles; resolve effective permissions. | . | Organizations | Team management and org-wide grants. | . | SCIM | An Organization’s identity provider inviting and removing its members (SCIM 2.0). | . | Tenancy | Where a Tenant’s data lives, and the (support-only) process to change it. | . | Billing | The Free/Standard subscription: a User’s or Organization’s plan, Stripe Checkout and Portal, and which members an Organization covers. | . | Audit | Query the audit log. | . | Webhooks | Subscribe to access-change events, including the required access.revoked. | . | Push Notifications | Alerts and updates to a User’s devices (APNs, FCM, Web Push) and their notification inbox: device registration, an Application’s push credentials, sending, and platform alerts. | . | API Keys | Service-to-service credentials — how billing or an app’s own backend authenticates. | . These pages specify the target contract for an API that does not yet exist. If you’re implementing against this, these are the shapes to build toward — check the repository’s actual code for what’s already real before assuming a page here is live. Calling this from an AI agent rather than writing HTTP calls by hand? See MCP Server — a tool-call interface generated from openapi.yaml, not a separate contract from the one on this page.

242.title: What the document covers
242.content: Operations are grouped by tag, and each tag matches an API Reference page that explains the rules behind it. | Tag | Operations | Prose reference | . | Meta | 1 | Conventions → Health check | . | Auth | 21 | Auth | . | Users | 10 | Users | . | Profiles | 4 | Profiles | . | Settings | 4 | Settings | . | Applications | 4 | Applications | . | Entitlements | 6 | Entitlements | . | Roles & Permissions | 10 | Roles & Permissions | . | Organizations | 14 | Organizations | . | Tenancy | 6 | Tenancy | . | Billing | 7 | Billing | . | Audit | 4 | Audit | . | Webhooks | 9 | Webhooks | . | Notifications | 17 | Push Notifications | . | API Keys | 6 | API Keys | . Some endpoints aren’t in the document’s paths, because they follow external standards instead: . | GET /.well-known/jwks.json and GET /.well-known/openid-configuration: signing keys and discovery, for verifying app tokens with any standard JWT library. See Auth → Signing keys. | /mcp: the MCP Server, generated from this document’s operationIds. | /scim/v2/…: SCIM 2.0 provisioning, following RFC 7644. | .

243.title: Authentication in the spec
243.content: The document declares one security scheme, bearerAuth (HTTP bearer), and applies it globally. The few operations that need no credential, such as GET /health, signup, and login, override it with security: []. The same header carries both credential types: . | Credential | Looks like | Used by | Get one from | . | User access token | A JWT | A person, or a client acting for them | POST /auth/login, /auth/signup, /auth/mfa/verify, or /auth/token/refresh | . | API Key | satk_live_… or satk_test_… | Your backend, service to service | API Keys | . Some operations accept only one of the two. For example, every Billing operation returns 400 user_token_required when called with an API Key. The operation’s description says so, and its prose page lists the permission it requires. A satk_test_… key works against the same base URL but only ever sees test-mode records. There’s no separate sandbox host. See Conventions → Authentication.

244.title: Reading an operation
244.content: Each operation in the document follows the same conventions, so you only need to learn them once: . | operationId is stable and namespaced (entitlements.grant, users.get). Generated clients use it for method names, and the MCP server uses it for tool names. Renaming one counts as a breaking change. | Errors all share one shape ({"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}, with the request id in the X-Request-Id header) through the shared responses BadRequest, Unauthorized, Forbidden, NotFound, Conflict, Unprocessable, TooManyRequests, and ServiceUnavailable. Branch on error.code, never on message. See Conventions → Errors. | Pagination uses the shared Limit and Cursor parameters (limit 1–100, default 25). See Conventions → Pagination. | Idempotency. Operations that create something take the Idempotency-Key header. Some require it, and their descriptions say which. See Conventions → Idempotency. | Concurrency. Single-resource responses carry an ETag header. Send it back as If-Match on PATCH to avoid overwriting someone else’s change. See Conventions → Concurrency. | IDs are typed by prefix (usr_, ent_, org_, …). Most are a prefix plus a ULID. Application and Role ids are derived (app_<slug>, role_<slug>_<name>). See Conventions → IDs. | me can stand in for your own User id in any /users/{id} path. See Conventions → Addressing yourself. | . Vendor extensions . | Extension | Values | Meaning | . | x-substratal-destructive | always | conditional | The operation destroys or irreversibly changes data. It’s rejected for API Keys created with restrict_destructive: true, and the MCP server marks it destructiveHint. See API Keys → Agent keys. | . | x-substratal-destructive-when | a description of the request | With conditional, only requests matching this are destructive. The rest of the operation stays callable with a restricted key. | . | x-substratal-phase | mvp, phase2, phase3 | The Roadmap phase the operation ships in. | . Code generators ignore these extensions, so they’re safe to leave in.

245.title: Generate a client
245.content: Any OpenAPI 3.1 tool works. A few common ones: . # TypeScript types, with no runtime dependency npx openapi-typescript https://compositecode.github.io/substratalapps.com/versions/1.7.14/openapi.yaml -o substratal.d.ts # Go: types and a client (this is what the reference implementation uses for its server side) go run github.com/oapi-codegen/oapi-codegen/v2/cmd/oapi-codegen@latest \ -generate types,client -package substratal openapi.yaml > substratal.gen.go # Any of 50+ languages npx @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli generate -i openapi.yaml -g python -o ./substratal-python . To explore by hand, import openapi.yaml into Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, or any other tool that reads OpenAPI. The Interactive Reference also has “Try it out” built in, against a local devserver.

246.title: Validate your integration
